You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

**[ARTICLE 7 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Definition of Confidential Information**

\"**Confidential Information**\" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the \"**Disclosing Party**\") to the other Party (the \"**Receiving Party**\") in connection with this Agreement, whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically, or by any other means, and whether or not marked or designated as \"confidential,\" \"proprietary,\" or with any similar legend, that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Confidential Information includes: (a) business plans, strategies, forecasts, and financial information; (b) technical information, including source code, algorithms, model architectures, model weights, training data, APIs, and system designs; (c) trade secrets; (d) customer lists, supplier lists, and pricing information; (e) product roadmaps and development plans; and (f) the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including all pricing, fee, and commercial terms. Customer Data shall be deemed Confidential Information of Customer regardless of whether it is marked or designated as confidential.

Confidential Information shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of or breach by the Receiving Party; (ii) was already known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records; (iii) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party without restriction on disclosure and without breach of any obligation of confidentiality owed to the Disclosing Party; or (iv) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records.

**Section 7.2 --- Obligations**

The Receiving Party shall: (a) hold the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) not disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to any third party except as expressly permitted under Section 7.3; (c) use the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information solely for the purposes of performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Agreement; and (d) protect the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information using measures that are no less protective than those used by the Receiving Party to protect its own most sensitive confidential information, but in no event less than a reasonable standard of care.

The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 7 shall remain in effect during the Term and for a period of five (5) years following the date of disclosure; provided, however, that the confidentiality obligations with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law shall continue for so long as such information remains a trade secret.

**Section 7.3 --- Permitted Disclosures**

The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to its employees, officers, directors, agents, contractors, consultants, advisors, and Affiliates who have a legitimate need to know such information for the purposes of this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 7 (collectively, \"**Authorized Recipients**\"). The Receiving Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 7 by its Authorized Recipients.

The Receiving Party may also disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or other legal process, provided that the Receiving Party: (a) provides the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice of such requirement (to the extent legally permitted) so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy; (b) cooperates with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party\'s expense, in seeking such protective order or other remedy; and (c) discloses only the minimum amount of Confidential Information necessary to comply with such requirement. Any Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to a legal compulsion shall retain its confidential status for all other purposes under this Agreement.

**Section 9.1 --- Uptime**

Vendor shall maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the \"**Uptime SLA**\"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:

> **Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100**

For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"**Downtime**\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).

Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours\' advance written notice to Customer\'s designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.

**Section 9.2 --- Latency**

Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.

**Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy**

Vendor shall maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above zero point ninety-four (F1 ≥ 0.94), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset established during the implementation process, following the conclusion of the Stabilization Period. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer\'s production document processing workloads.

During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.

**Section 9.4 --- Service Credits**

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA, API Latency target, or Model Accuracy target in any applicable measurement period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a \"**Service Credit**\"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the SLA failure occurred.

Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against Customer\'s next invoice(s) under this Agreement . If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed thirty percent (30%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year. Service Credits are not Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5.

Priya,

endStream context so clearly. I understand that the real-time consumer experi=
ence is central to TechNova's product value proposition, and I want to make s=
ure we find a path that works for both sides on the remaining open items.

I've gone back to our infrastructure team on this, and p95 =E2=89=A4 450 ms r=
emains our engineering team's committed floor. This number has been validated=
against our current architecture and the projected traffic volumes we've bee=
n working from (~52M calls/year against the 40M included tier).
I hear you that 400 ms is a product requirement on your side, not an aspirati=
onal number. The challenge on our end is that committing to 400 ms contractua=
lly at this stage would expose Meridian to credit liability on a performance =
target we cannot guarantee at scale from day one =E2=80=94 particularly befor=
e we've had the benefit of observing real production traffic patterns and opt=
imizing accordingly.
What I'd like to propose: let's hold at 450 ms as the contractual commitment =
for the initial term, with an agreement to revisit the latency target at the =
first annual review once we have meaningful production data in hand. I'm also=
open to distinguishing between aspirational targets (which we can track and =
report against collaboratively) and contractual commitments (which carry cred=
it exposure). That distinction may give your product team the visibility they=
need while keeping our credit framework grounded in what we can guarantee to=
day.

s to close the gap further, we're happy to scope that =E2=80=94 but as I note=
d previously, those infrastructure investments would need to be reflected in =
pricing, and I'd rather we nail that down as a separate workstream than hold =
up the MSA.

a concrete framework rather than just going back and forth on the number.

ume, and representativeness of Customer training data that has not yet been i=
ngested. Committing to 0.94 before we've seen the data would be making a prom=
ise we can't back up with engineering confidence, and I don't think either of=
us wants that in the contract.
What I'd propose instead is a ramp mechanism:
- **At Go-Live (October 1, 2025):** F1 =E2=89=A5 0.90 as the contractual SLA =
floor.
- **Post-stabilization (approximately late December 2025 / early January 2026=
=E2=80=94 90 days after Go-Live):** The F1 target increases to a higher cont=
ractual floor. We're willing to entertain F1 =E2=89=A5 0.94 for this phase, p=
rovided TechNova delivers sufficient training data during the implementation =
period per a mutually agreed data delivery schedule.
This gives both sides a realistic contractual framework: you get the accuracy=
target your product team needs for regulated lending, and we get the runway =
to fine-tune on real data before we're on the hook for that number. I think t=
his also aligns with how the model will actually perform in practice =E2=80=
=94 it's going to get better as we train on your data, and the contract shoul=
d reflect that trajectory.
Happy to discuss the specifics of what "sufficient training data" means =E2=
=80=94 that's a conversation for our respective technical teams, and we can d=
efine it in the SOW.
**SLA Credit Caps**
You asked for our counter on credits, so here it is: Meridian's position is c=
redits capped at 15% of monthly fees, which works out to $30,000/month agains=
t the $200,000 monthly platform fee. Your Draft 2 proposed 30% ($60,000/month=
Our rationale: credit exposure above 15% effectively becomes a penalty regime=
rather than a service-level incentive mechanism. Meridian's standard enterpr=
ise SLA credit structure across our customer base runs 10=E2=80=9315%, and we=
've found that range strikes the right balance between meaningful accountabil=
ity and sustainable vendor economics. At 30%, the credit tail starts to wag t=
he commercial dog, and frankly it creates perverse incentives on our side to =
over-engineer margins of safety rather than invest in the product improvement=
s that actually benefit your end users.
That said, I'm open to discussing the credit tier structure and calculation m=
ethodology =E2=80=94 how credits accrue across different SLA dimensions (upti=
me vs. latency vs. accuracy), whether they're additive or capped in aggregate=
, measurement windows, and so on. There's room to be creative here, and I'd r=
ather we get the mechanics right than just negotiate a top-line percentage in=
isolation.
**Termination for Chronic SLA Failure**
I anticipate this will be on your list, and we're open to discussing a termin=
ation trigger for persistent SLA misses. Our preference is to structure this =
around a threshold of consecutive months of material SLA failure (e.g., X con=
secutive months) rather than a rolling aggregate methodology, which in our ex=
perience can produce termination triggers that don't reflect the actual state=
of the service relationship. Happy to flesh this out on the joint call.
**Next Steps**
I think we're making good progress narrowing the business-level gaps. Here's =
what I'd suggest:
1. Let's try to get aligned on the remaining open items (latency, F1 ramp, cr=
edit caps, termination trigger) over the next week or so at the business leve=
l.
2. Once we have handshake positions, let's loop in the legal teams =E2=80=94 =
Simone Delacroix on our side and Derek Chalmers on yours =E2=80=94 to transla=
te into contract language.
3. I'd propose a joint business-legal call the week of May 19 to align on any=
remaining open items and ensure Draft 3 reflects agreed positions. Target fo=
r Draft 3 circulation: May 16.
4. That keeps us on track for the June 15 target execution date and July 1 Ef=
fective Date, which I believe is still achievable if we can close these gaps =
in the next two weeks.
Looking forward to your thoughts on the ramp mechanism in particular =E2=80=
=94 I think that may be the key to unlocking the accuracy discussion.
Best regards,
Jonas Ekberg
Chief Revenue Officer
Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC

**IP Ownership / Licensing Construct**
TechNova formally reserves its right to continue to advocate for full Custome=
r ownership of fine-tuned weights and Customer-Trained Adaptations, and we ex=

ative or fallback. That said, we are willing to explore the irrevocable, perp=
etual, royalty-free license construct as a working framework, provided it is =

terial uncured breach exceeding 60 days, and cessation of product support; and

of the licensed adapter weights post-termination.
Rachel will reflect this construct in Draft 3 as the primary working framewor=
k while preserving TechNova's ownership position in brackets as an alternativ=
e.
**AI-Output Indemnity**
Understood that Meridian needs time for internal review with product, enginee=
ring, and insurance. However, I want to flag that this is a critical provisio=
n for TechNova. We are integrating MeridianIQ outputs directly into a consume=
r-facing lending platform, and the risk allocation on downstream third-party =
claims needs to be addressed squarely in the agreement.

culation on May 16. I want to be transparent: without adequate AI-output inde=
mnity coverage, TechNova would need to revisit the overall risk allocation fr=
amework, including the liability cap and super-cap structure we've been discu=
ssing. These provisions do not exist in isolation.
**Liability Cap**
The parties remain apart on the general cap =E2=80=94 TechNova at $4.8M (2=C3=
=97 annual fees) and Meridian at $2.4M (1=C3=97 annual fees). There may be ro=
om for compromise, but I'm not in a position to float a specific number until=

e super-cap. For now, I can confirm that the super-cap concept at $7.2M for I=
P indemnity and data breach carve-outs is worth continued discussion, alongsi=
de the uncapped treatment of willful misconduct and gross negligence, which I=
understand to be agreed.

Rachel Mu=C3=B1oz at Kirkstead & Yao is preparing Draft 3 with a target circu=
lation date of **May 16, 2025**. Draft 3 will use TechNova's Draft 2 (dated A=
pril 21, 2025) as the base document, with Draft 2 tracked changes accepted to=
produce a clean base, and will show K&Y's new tracked changes against that c=
lean version. The markup will incorporate agreed positions, propose compromis=
e language on partially resolved items, and flag remaining open issues with a=
nnotations. We would ask that Meridian and Capstone Bridger turn comments pro=
mptly upon receipt to maintain the June 15 execution target.
**Joint Call =E2=80=93 Week of May 19**
Confirmed. I'd propose the following agenda for the call:
1. AI-output indemnity
2. Governing law / dispute resolution
3. Liability cap / super-cap
4. De-identified data certification requirement
5. Tech E&O insurance limits
6. Latency and accuracy SLA targets

8. Escrow agent selection and scope

g poll early next week.
We've made good progress this week, Simone, and I appreciate the substantive =
engagement from your side. It's important that we maintain this momentum =E2=
=80=94 the initial term commencement on July 1, 2025, and Go-Live on October =
1, 2025, don't leave us a lot of runway for extended back-and-forth on the re=
maining open items. Let's aim to close as much as we can in the next two week=
s.
Best regards,
