lines.text: **[DATA PROCESSING ADDENDUM]{.underline}**
**to the Master Services Agreement / Vendor Agreement**
**by and between**
**and**

This Data Processing Addendum (\"DPA\") is incorporated into and forms part of the \[**\_\_\_**\] (the \"Agreement\") dated \[**\_\_\_**\] between the parties identified above (each, a \"Party\" and collectively, the \"Parties\"). This DPA establishes the terms and conditions under which Vendor will Process Personal Information on behalf of Company in connection with the services provided under the Agreement. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement.
**[Recitals]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS,** the Parties have entered into the Agreement referenced above, pursuant to which Vendor provides certain services to Company (also referred to herein as \"TechNova\") or its affiliates, as more fully described in the Agreement;

**WHEREAS,** the performance of the Agreement involves Vendor\'s Processing of Personal Information on behalf of Company, and such Processing activities are integral to the delivery of the services contemplated under the Agreement;

**WHEREAS,** the Parties desire to establish their respective obligations regarding the protection of Personal Information in compliance with all Applicable Data Protection Laws, including but not limited to the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 (\"CCPA\"), as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020 (\"CPRA\"), the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (\"GLBA\"), and all other applicable federal, state, and international data protection and privacy laws and regulations;
**WHEREAS,** this DPA sets forth the terms and conditions governing such Processing and supplements the Agreement with respect to the Parties\' data protection obligations; and

**WHEREAS,** in the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the provisions of this DPA and the provisions of the Agreement, this DPA shall prevail with respect to the Processing of Personal Information to the extent of such conflict or inconsistency.

**NOW, THEREFORE,** in consideration of the mutual promises set forth herein and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
**[Article 1 --- Definitions]{.underline}**
For the purposes of this DPA, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

**1.1 \"Applicable Data Protection Laws\"** means all federal, state, local, and international laws, statutes, regulations, rules, ordinances, and regulatory guidance governing the Processing of Personal Information that are applicable to either Party\'s performance under the Agreement, including without limitation: (a) the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.100 *et seq.*), as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020 (\"CPRA\"); (b) the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (15 U.S.C. § 6801 *et seq.*) and its implementing regulations, including the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314); (c) the California Financial Information Privacy Act (Cal. Fin. Code § 4050 *et seq.*); (d) any other applicable state consumer privacy statutes; and (e) all regulations, guidance, and opinions issued by competent regulatory authorities interpreting any of the foregoing, in each case as amended, superseded, or replaced from time to time.
**1.2 \"Business\"** has the meaning ascribed to such term under CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(d), and as used in this DPA refers to Company.

**1.3 \"Business Purpose\"** has the meaning ascribed to such term under CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(e), and refers to the specific purposes for which Personal Information is disclosed by Company to Vendor, as described in Exhibit C attached hereto. For the avoidance of doubt, \"Business Purpose\" includes any use of Personal Information that is necessary to perform the services set forth in the Agreement, including auditing, detecting security incidents, debugging, short-term transient use, performing services on behalf of Company, internal research for technological development, and activities to verify or maintain the quality or safety of a service, all as further described in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(e).

**1.4 \"Consumer\"** means a natural person who is a California resident, as defined under CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(i), or any individual whose Personal Information is subject to Applicable Data Protection Laws. The term \"Consumer\" includes \"Data Subject\" where applicable under Applicable Data Protection Laws, and shall be construed broadly to encompass any individual afforded rights with respect to their Personal Information under any Applicable Data Protection Law.

**1.5 \"Controller\"** means the entity that, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of Processing Personal Information. As used in this DPA, \"Controller\" refers to Company.

**1.6 \"Data Breach\"** means any unauthorized access to, or unauthorized acquisition, disclosure, use, destruction, alteration, or loss of, Personal Information, whether in electronic or physical form, including any \"breach of the security of the system\" as defined under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.29 and Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82, and any event that triggers notification obligations under any Applicable Data Protection Law. The term \"Data Breach\" encompasses both confirmed breaches and reasonably suspected breaches.

**1.7 \"De-Identified Data\"** means information that cannot reasonably be used to infer information about, or otherwise be linked to, a particular Consumer or household, provided that a business that uses De-Identified Data: (a) has implemented technical safeguards that prohibit re-identification of the Consumer to whom the information may pertain; (b) has implemented business processes that specifically prohibit re-identification of the information; (c) has implemented business processes to prevent inadvertent release of De-Identified Data; and (d) makes no attempt to re-identify the information, all in accordance with the requirements of Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and as further described in Article 10 of this DPA.

**1.8 \"GLBA\"** means the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 6801--6809, and its implementing regulations, including the Federal Trade Commission\'s Standards for Safeguarding Customer Information (the \"FTC Safeguards Rule,\" 16 C.F.R. Part 314), the Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards, and any successor regulations or amendments thereto.

**1.9 \"Personal Information\"** means information that identifies, relates to, describes, is reasonably capable of being associated with, or could reasonably be linked, directly or indirectly, with a particular Consumer or household, as defined under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(v). The term \"Personal Information\" also includes \"Nonpublic Personal Information\" as defined under GLBA (15 U.S.C. § 6809(4)) and its implementing regulations, where such information is Processed in connection with the services provided under the Agreement. Personal Information does not include publicly available information, De-Identified Data, or aggregate consumer information, to the extent such exclusions are recognized under Applicable Data Protection Laws.

**1.10 \"Processing\"** (and \"Process,\" \"Processed\") means any operation or set of operations that is performed on Personal Information or on sets of Personal Information, whether or not by automated means, including but not limited to collection, recording, organization, structuring, storage, adaptation, alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination, or otherwise making available, alignment, combination, restriction, erasure, or destruction, as referenced in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(y).

**1.11 \"Processor\"** means an entity that Processes Personal Information on behalf of the Controller. As used in this DPA, \"Processor\" refers to Vendor in its capacity as a service provider under the Agreement.

**1.12 \"Service Provider\"** has the meaning ascribed to such term under CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag), and refers to Vendor in its capacity under the Agreement. For purposes of this DPA, Vendor is a Service Provider that receives Personal Information from Company for a Business Purpose pursuant to a written contract that satisfies the requirements of the CCPA and CPRA.

**1.13 \"Sub-Processor\"** means any third party (other than Vendor\'s employees) engaged by Vendor to Process Personal Information on behalf of Company in connection with the services provided under the Agreement. A Sub-Processor includes any subcontractor, agent, or other downstream service provider to which Vendor delegates any portion of the Processing activities contemplated under this DPA.

**1.14 \"Technical and Organizational Measures\"** or **\"TOMs\"** means the administrative, technical, and physical security measures implemented by Vendor to protect Personal Information against unauthorized or unlawful Processing and against accidental loss, destruction, damage, alteration, or disclosure, as more fully described in Exhibit A to this DPA.

**1.15 Incorporation of Agreement Definitions.** All terms defined in the Agreement that are used but not separately defined in this DPA shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement. In the event of any conflict between the definitions set forth in this DPA and the definitions set forth in the Agreement, the definitions in this DPA shall control with respect to matters relating to the Processing of Personal Information.
**[Article 2 --- Roles and Scope of Processing]{.underline}**

**2.1 Designation of Roles.** With respect to Personal Information Processed under the Agreement, Company shall act as the Business and Controller, and Vendor shall act as the Service Provider and Processor. Each Party shall comply with the obligations applicable to it in its respective role under Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor acknowledges and agrees that it is a \"service provider\" as defined under the CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag), and shall act in accordance with the duties and restrictions applicable to service providers under the CCPA and CPRA.

**2.2 Purpose Limitation.** Vendor shall Process Personal Information solely on behalf of Company and only for the specific Business Purposes identified in Exhibit C to this DPA. Vendor shall not Process Personal Information for any purpose that is incompatible with the Business Purposes specified herein without the prior written consent of Company. Any additional Processing activities beyond those described in Exhibit C shall require a written amendment to this DPA executed by both Parties in accordance with Section 14.3.

**2.3 Processing Description.** The subject matter, duration, nature, and purpose of Processing, the categories of Personal Information Processed, and the categories of Consumers whose Personal Information is Processed are described in Exhibit C (Processing Description) attached to this DPA. Exhibit C is incorporated herein by reference and forms an integral part of this DPA. Company may update Exhibit C from time to time in writing to reflect changes in the scope of services under the Agreement, and Vendor shall comply with any such updates promptly upon receipt.

**2.4 No Consideration for Personal Information.** Vendor acknowledges and agrees that it does not receive Personal Information as consideration for the services provided under the Agreement. Personal Information is disclosed by Company to Vendor solely for the Business Purposes described in this DPA and Exhibit C. The exchange of Personal Information does not constitute a \"sale\" or \"sharing\" of Personal Information within the meaning of the CCPA or CPRA.

**2.5 No Ownership Interest.** Nothing in this DPA or the Agreement confers upon Vendor any ownership interest, license, or other proprietary right in or to the Personal Information. Vendor acknowledges that Company retains all rights, title, and interest in and to the Personal Information at all times. Vendor\'s right to Process Personal Information is limited solely to the rights expressly granted under this DPA and the Agreement, and such right shall terminate upon the expiration or termination of the Agreement, subject to the data return and deletion obligations set forth in Article 11.
**[Article 3 --- Processing Instructions and Restrictions]{.underline}**

**3.1 Documented Instructions.** Vendor shall Process Personal Information only in accordance with Company\'s documented instructions as set forth in this DPA, Exhibit C, and any subsequent written instructions provided by Company from time to time. Company\'s initial instructions are set forth in Exhibit C and are deemed effective as of the effective date of this DPA. Vendor shall not deviate from Company\'s documented instructions without prior written authorization from Company. If Vendor believes that additional Processing is necessary for reasons other than those instructed by Company, Vendor shall promptly inform Company of such necessity before commencing such Processing, unless prohibited from doing so by Applicable Data Protection Laws, in which case Vendor shall notify Company of the relevant legal requirement to the extent permitted by law.

**3.2 Prohibition on Sale, Sharing, and Unauthorized Disclosure.** Vendor shall not sell, share, rent, release, disclose, disseminate, make available, transfer, or otherwise communicate orally, in writing, or by electronic or other means, Personal Information to any third party for any purpose other than the specific Business Purposes set forth in this DPA and the Agreement. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Vendor shall not \"sell\" or \"share\" Personal Information, as those terms are defined in the CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.140(ad) and 1798.140(ah), respectively.

**3.3 No Unauthorized Retention, Use, or Disclosure.** Vendor shall not retain, use, or disclose Personal Information for any commercial purpose other than providing the services specified in the Agreement and for the Business Purposes identified in Exhibit C. Vendor shall not retain, use, or disclose Personal Information outside of the direct business relationship between Vendor and Company. For the avoidance of doubt, Vendor shall not use Personal Information received from Company to build or enhance profiles concerning Consumers, to advertise or market products or services to Consumers, or for any purpose unrelated to the provision of the services under the Agreement.

**3.4 Prohibition on Combining Personal Information.** Vendor shall not combine Personal Information received from, or on behalf of, Company with Personal Information that Vendor: (a) receives from, or on behalf of, another person or persons; or (b) collects from its own interaction with Consumers, except as expressly permitted under CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(e)(6), which permits combining Personal Information to the extent necessary to detect data security incidents or to protect against fraudulent or illegal activity, provided that such combining is performed solely to the extent reasonably necessary and proportionate to achieving such purposes.

**3.5 Notification of Unlawful Instructions.** Vendor shall promptly inform Company in writing if, in Vendor\'s reasonable opinion, an instruction from Company infringes Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall not be required to comply with any instruction that it reasonably believes to be unlawful, and shall await further written instructions from Company before proceeding. In the event of a disagreement between the Parties regarding the lawfulness of an instruction, the Parties shall consult in good faith to resolve the matter. Vendor shall document any notification provided under this Section and retain such documentation for the term of this DPA.

**3.6 Confidentiality of Personnel.** Vendor shall ensure that all persons authorized to Process Personal Information on Vendor\'s behalf, including employees, contractors, agents, and other personnel, have committed themselves to binding obligations of confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality. Vendor shall ensure that such personnel Process Personal Information only in accordance with Vendor\'s instructions, which shall be consistent with Company\'s instructions as set forth in this DPA. Vendor shall provide regular training to its personnel regarding the obligations imposed by this DPA and Applicable Data Protection Laws, and shall maintain records of such training.
**[Article 4 --- Sub-Processor Management]{.underline}**

**4.1 Prior Written Consent Required.** Vendor shall not engage any Sub-Processor to Process Personal Information on behalf of Company without obtaining Company\'s prior written consent. Such consent may be granted on a specific or general basis. If Company provides general authorization, Vendor shall comply with the notification and objection procedures set forth in Sections 4.3 and 4.4 below before engaging any new Sub-Processor or replacing an existing Sub-Processor.

**4.2 Approved Sub-Processors.** A list of Sub-Processors approved by Company as of the effective date of this DPA is set forth in Exhibit B. Company hereby grants specific written consent for each Sub-Processor identified in Exhibit B as of the effective date of this DPA. Vendor represents and warrants that, as of the effective date, the Sub-Processors listed in Exhibit B are the only Sub-Processors engaged by Vendor to Process Personal Information on behalf of Company.

**4.3 New Sub-Processor Notification.** Prior to engaging any new Sub-Processor or replacing an existing Sub-Processor, Vendor shall provide Company with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice. Such notice shall include: (a) the identity of the proposed Sub-Processor, including its legal name and principal place of business; (b) a description of the nature and scope of the Processing activities to be performed by the proposed Sub-Processor; (c) the location(s) where Processing will occur; and (d) an explanation of how the proposed Sub-Processor will comply with the obligations set forth in this DPA. Vendor shall update Exhibit B promptly upon the engagement of any new Sub-Processor approved by Company.

**4.4 Company Objection Rights.** Company shall have the right to object to the engagement of a proposed Sub-Processor by providing written notice of its objection to Vendor within fifteen (15) days of receiving Vendor\'s notification under Section 4.3. Company\'s objection notice shall set forth the reasonable grounds for objection. Upon receipt of an objection, the Parties shall engage in good-faith discussions to resolve the matter, which may include Vendor proposing an alternative Sub-Processor or implementing additional safeguards. If the Parties are unable to resolve the objection within thirty (30) days of Company\'s objection notice, Company shall have the right to terminate the affected services under the Agreement without penalty, liability, or early-termination fee, by providing written notice to Vendor. Such termination shall be effective upon the date specified in Company\'s termination notice, which shall be no less than thirty (30) days from the date of such notice, and Vendor shall comply with the data return and deletion obligations set forth in Article 11 with respect to the terminated services.

**4.5 Flow-Down Obligations.** Vendor shall impose on each Sub-Processor, by way of a written agreement, data protection obligations that are no less protective of Personal Information than those set forth in this DPA. Such written agreement shall include, at a minimum: (a) the obligation to Process Personal Information only in accordance with Company\'s documented instructions; (b) the obligation to implement appropriate Technical and Organizational Measures; (c) the obligation to cooperate with audits and inspections; (d) the obligation to assist in responding to Consumer rights requests; (e) Data Breach notification obligations; and (f) data return and deletion obligations upon termination. Vendor shall provide Company with copies of its Sub-Processor agreements, or relevant excerpts thereof (which may be redacted to remove commercially sensitive information not related to data protection), upon Company\'s reasonable request.

**4.6 Vendor Liability for Sub-Processors.** Vendor shall remain fully liable to Company for the acts and omissions of its Sub-Processors with respect to the Processing of Personal Information as if such acts and omissions were Vendor\'s own. Vendor\'s engagement of a Sub-Processor shall not relieve Vendor of any of its obligations under this DPA or the Agreement. If a Sub-Processor fails to fulfill its data protection obligations, Vendor shall be directly and primarily liable to Company for the performance of the Sub-Processor\'s obligations.

**4.7 Company Audit Rights over Sub-Processors.** Company\'s right to audit Sub-Processors shall be exercised in accordance with Article 12. Company may audit Sub-Processors directly or may direct Vendor to conduct such audits on Company\'s behalf and provide the results to Company. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to include in its Sub-Processor agreements provisions allowing Company or its designee to exercise audit rights over the Sub-Processor\'s Processing activities related to Company\'s Personal Information.
**[Article 5 --- Data Security Requirements]{.underline}**

**5.1 General Security Obligation.** Vendor shall implement and maintain appropriate Technical and Organizational Measures to protect Personal Information against unauthorized or unlawful Processing and against accidental loss, destruction, damage, alteration, or disclosure. The TOMs shall be appropriate to the risk, taking into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation, and the nature, scope, context, and purposes of Processing, as well as the likelihood and severity of harm to Consumers. The specific TOMs in effect as of the effective date of this DPA are described in Exhibit A. Vendor shall ensure that such measures provide a level of security appropriate to the sensitivity of the Personal Information being Processed.
**5.2 Specific Security Requirements.** Without limiting the generality of Section 5.1, Vendor shall implement and maintain the following security measures at a minimum:

> \(a\) **Encryption at Rest.** All Personal Information stored by Vendor, whether on Vendor\'s own systems or on systems operated by Sub-Processors, shall be encrypted at rest using Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) with a key length of 256 bits (AES-256) or an equivalent or stronger encryption standard approved by Company in writing.

> \(b\) **Encryption in Transit.** All Personal Information transmitted by Vendor, including transmission over public networks, internal networks, and between Vendor and Sub-Processors, shall be encrypted in transit using Transport Layer Security (TLS) version 1.2 or higher, or an equivalent or stronger encryption protocol approved by Company in writing.

> \(c\) **Access Controls.** Vendor shall implement and maintain role-based access controls (RBAC) and adhere to the principle of least privilege, ensuring that access to Personal Information is limited to those personnel who require such access to perform their job functions in connection with the services under the Agreement. Access rights shall be reviewed and updated on a regular basis, and no less frequently than quarterly.

> \(d\) **Multi-Factor Authentication.** Vendor shall require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users accessing systems, applications, or environments that Process Personal Information, including remote access, administrative access, and access to cloud-based services.

> \(e\) **Vulnerability Assessments and Penetration Testing.** Vendor shall conduct regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing of its systems and infrastructure that Process Personal Information. Vulnerability assessments shall be conducted at least quarterly, and penetration testing shall be conducted at least annually by a qualified independent third party. Vendor shall provide Company with executive summaries of such assessments and tests upon request, along with remediation plans for any identified vulnerabilities rated as critical or high severity.

> \(f\) **Intrusion Detection and Monitoring.** Vendor shall implement and maintain intrusion detection systems (IDS) and intrusion prevention systems (IPS) to monitor network traffic and detect potential security threats to systems that Process Personal Information. Vendor shall maintain a security operations function capable of monitoring and responding to security alerts on a continuous, 24/7 basis.

> \(g\) **Logging and Audit Trails.** Vendor shall maintain comprehensive logging and audit trails for all access to, and actions performed on, Personal Information, including user authentication, data access, data modification, and data deletion events. Logs shall be maintained in a tamper-evident manner and retained for a period of not less than twelve (12) months, or such longer period as required by Applicable Data Protection Laws. Logs shall be made available to Company upon reasonable request and in connection with audits conducted under Article 12.

**5.3 SOC 2 Type II Certification.** Vendor shall obtain and maintain a current Service Organization Control (SOC) 2 Type II report, prepared by an independent certified public accounting firm in accordance with the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) Trust Services Criteria, covering at a minimum the Security, Availability, and Confidentiality trust services criteria. Vendor shall provide a copy of the most recent SOC 2 Type II report to Company upon execution of this DPA, and thereafter on an annual basis within thirty (30) days of Vendor\'s receipt of each updated report. Vendor shall promptly notify Company of any material exceptions, qualifications, or findings of non-compliance identified in any SOC 2 Type II report, along with Vendor\'s plans and timelines for remediation.

**5.4 Notification of Material Security Changes.** Vendor shall promptly notify Company in writing of any material changes to its Technical and Organizational Measures that may adversely affect the security, confidentiality, integrity, or availability of Personal Information. Such notification shall be provided at least thirty (30) days in advance of the planned change, or as soon as reasonably practicable in the case of emergency changes. Company reserves the right to review and approve or reject any such changes, and Vendor shall not implement any material adverse change without Company\'s prior written consent.

**5.5 Additional Security Specifications.** \[**\_\_\_**\] *(This field is reserved for engagement-specific security requirements to be mutually agreed upon by the Parties and documented herein or in a separately executed addendum. Such additional requirements, if any, shall be incorporated herein by reference and shall have the same force and effect as the security obligations set forth in this Article 5.)*
**[Article 6 --- CCPA Service Provider Certification]{.underline}**

**6.1 Understanding and Compliance Certification.** Vendor hereby certifies that it understands and will comply with the restrictions, obligations, and requirements applicable to service providers under the CCPA, as amended by the CPRA, and as set forth in this DPA. Vendor acknowledges that compliance with the CCPA is an essential component of its obligations under this DPA and the Agreement.

**6.2 Statutory Service Provider Certification.** In accordance with the requirements of Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag) and the regulations promulgated thereunder, Vendor hereby certifies each of the following:

> \(a\) Vendor certifies that it shall not sell or share Personal Information received from Company, and Vendor has no actual knowledge that it sells or shares Personal Information received from Company;

> \(b\) Vendor certifies that it shall not retain, use, or disclose Personal Information received from Company for any purpose other than for the specific Business Purposes set forth in the Agreement and this DPA, including retaining, using, or disclosing Personal Information for a commercial purpose other than providing the services specified in the Agreement, and as permitted under the CCPA and CPRA;

> \(c\) Vendor certifies that it shall not retain, use, or disclose Personal Information received from Company outside of the direct business relationship between Vendor and Company, except as expressly permitted by the CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(e)(6), or as otherwise authorized in writing by Company; and

> \(d\) Vendor certifies that it shall comply with all applicable provisions of the CCPA and CPRA, including all regulations promulgated by the California Privacy Protection Agency, as they may be amended from time to time.

**6.3 Company\'s Right to Ensure Compliance.** Vendor grants Company the right, upon reasonable notice, to take reasonable and appropriate steps to help ensure that Vendor uses Personal Information received from Company in a manner consistent with Company\'s obligations under the CCPA and CPRA. Such steps may include, without limitation, requesting information about Vendor\'s Processing activities, conducting audits or assessments in accordance with Article 12, and requiring Vendor to implement additional safeguards or remedial measures. Vendor shall cooperate fully with Company in connection with any such steps.

**6.4 Notification of Inability to Comply.** Vendor shall promptly notify Company if Vendor determines that it can no longer meet its obligations under the CCPA or CPRA, or if any change in Applicable Data Protection Laws materially affects Vendor\'s ability to comply with its obligations under this Article. Upon receipt of such notification, Company shall have the right to take reasonable and appropriate steps to stop and remediate any unauthorized use of Personal Information, which may include directing Vendor to cease Processing Personal Information, suspending the transfer of Personal Information to Vendor, and/or terminating the Agreement or the affected services thereunder. Vendor shall bear all costs and expenses associated with Vendor\'s failure to comply with its obligations under this Article.
**[Article 7 --- GLBA Safeguards Compliance]{.underline}**

**7.1 Applicability.** To the extent that Vendor receives, maintains, or Processes Personal Information that constitutes \"customer information\" or \"Nonpublic Personal Information\" as defined under GLBA and its implementing regulations, Vendor shall comply with the safeguards requirements of the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) and any other applicable GLBA requirements. The obligations set forth in this Article 7 are in addition to, and do not limit, the security obligations set forth in Article 5.

**7.2 Comprehensive Information Security Program.** Vendor shall develop, implement, and maintain a comprehensive written information security program that contains administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to: (a) ensure the security and confidentiality of Nonpublic Personal Information; (b) protect against any anticipated threats or hazards to the security or integrity of such information; and (c) protect against unauthorized access to or use of such information that could result in substantial harm or inconvenience to any Consumer. The safeguards shall be appropriate to the size and complexity of Vendor\'s operations, the nature and scope of Vendor\'s activities, and the sensitivity of the Nonpublic Personal Information at issue.

**7.3 Designated Qualified Individual.** Vendor shall designate a qualified individual responsible for overseeing, implementing, and enforcing Vendor\'s information security program. The qualified individual may be an employee, affiliate, or a third-party service provider, provided that, in the case of a third-party service provider, Vendor retains overall responsibility for oversight and direction of the information security program. Vendor shall provide Company with the name, title, and contact information of the designated qualified individual upon Company\'s request.

**7.4 Periodic Risk Assessments.** Vendor shall conduct periodic risk assessments, no less frequently than annually, that: (a) identify reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks to the security, confidentiality, and integrity of Nonpublic Personal Information that could result in the unauthorized disclosure, misuse, alteration, destruction, or other compromise of such information; (b) assess the sufficiency of any safeguards in place to control these risks; and (c) design and implement safeguards to control the risks identified through the risk assessment. Vendor shall adjust its information security program based on the results of each risk assessment and shall maintain documentation of each risk assessment and the resulting actions taken.

**7.5 Access Restriction.** Vendor shall restrict access to Nonpublic Personal Information to those authorized personnel who have a legitimate business need for such access in connection with the services provided under the Agreement. Vendor shall implement and maintain procedures for granting, modifying, and revoking access to Nonpublic Personal Information, including prompt revocation of access upon termination of employment or engagement of any authorized personnel.

**7.6 Evidence of Compliance.** Vendor shall provide evidence of its compliance with the GLBA Safeguards requirements set forth in this Article upon Company\'s reasonable request. Such evidence may include, without limitation: (a) copies of or summaries of Vendor\'s information security program; (b) results of risk assessments (which may be provided in summary or redacted form to protect Vendor\'s confidential security information); (c) evidence of security training and awareness programs; (d) certifications or attestation letters from Vendor\'s designated qualified individual; and (e) any relevant audit reports, including SOC 2 Type II reports. Vendor shall provide such evidence within thirty (30) days of Company\'s request.
**[Article 8 --- Data Breach Notification]{.underline}**

**8.1 Notification Obligation.** Vendor shall notify Company of any confirmed or reasonably suspected Data Breach involving Personal Information Processed by Vendor or its Sub-Processors on behalf of Company without undue delay and in no event later than seventy-two (72) hours after Vendor first becomes aware of such Data Breach. Vendor shall direct its notification to Company\'s Privacy Contact identified in Section 14.8, as well as any other contacts designated by Company for Data Breach notifications. Notification shall be made by telephone and confirmed in writing via email and, if available, through any incident management portal designated by Company.
**8.2 Content of Notification.** Vendor\'s notification to Company under Section 8.1 shall include, to the extent known at the time of notification and without unreasonable delay:

> \(a\) A description of the nature of the Data Breach, including the categories and approximate number of Consumers affected and the categories and approximate number of Personal Information records affected;
> \(b\) The name, title, telephone number, and email address of Vendor\'s designated point of contact from whom Company may obtain additional information regarding the Data Breach;
> \(c\) A description of the likely consequences of the Data Breach, including a preliminary assessment of the risk of harm to affected Consumers;
> \(d\) A description of the measures taken or proposed to be taken by Vendor to address the Data Breach, including measures to contain the breach, mitigate its effects, and prevent recurrence; and
> \(e\) Any other information that Company may reasonably require to evaluate the Data Breach and fulfill its obligations under Applicable Data Protection Laws.

If Vendor does not have complete information at the time of the initial notification, Vendor shall provide the information described above in phases without further undue delay, and shall supplement its initial notification as additional information becomes available.

**8.3 Ongoing Cooperation.** Vendor shall cooperate fully with Company in investigating, remediating, and responding to any Data Breach, including: (a) providing Company with updated information regarding the Data Breach as it becomes available; (b) assisting Company in identifying affected Consumers and the Personal Information compromised; (c) supporting Company\'s regulatory filings, Consumer notifications, and other response activities; (d) preserving and producing documents, records, and other materials relevant to the Data Breach investigation; and (e) making Vendor\'s personnel, systems, and facilities reasonably available to Company and its investigators, legal counsel, and forensic consultants.

**8.4 Containment and Remediation.** Upon becoming aware of a Data Breach, Vendor shall immediately take all reasonable and necessary steps to contain, investigate, and remediate the Data Breach, including: (a) isolating affected systems; (b) preserving forensic evidence; (c) identifying the root cause; (d) eradicating the threat; (e) restoring the integrity of affected systems and data; and (f) implementing measures to prevent recurrence. All such containment, investigation, and remediation activities shall be performed at Vendor\'s sole cost and expense.

**8.5 Notification Restrictions.** Vendor shall not notify any Consumer, regulatory authority, law enforcement agency, credit reporting agency, or any other third party of a Data Breach involving Company\'s Personal Information without Company\'s prior written consent, unless Vendor is required to make such notification under Applicable Data Protection Laws, in which case Vendor shall: (a) notify Company of such legal requirement prior to making the notification, to the extent permitted by law; (b) coordinate with Company regarding the timing, content, and method of such notification; and (c) provide Company with a copy of any notification prior to its issuance, to the extent practicable.

**8.6 Preservation of Records and Evidence.** Vendor shall preserve all records, logs, files, data, communications, and other evidence related to a Data Breach in a secure and tamper-evident manner. Vendor shall not alter, destroy, or dispose of any such evidence without Company\'s prior written consent. Vendor shall make all such records and evidence available to Company and its authorized representatives upon request, at no additional cost to Company.

**8.7 Non-Exclusivity of Notification Obligations.** Vendor\'s notification obligations under this Article 8 are in addition to, and do not replace, modify, or limit, any notification obligations that Vendor may have under Applicable Data Protection Laws, the Agreement, or any other contractual arrangement between the Parties. Vendor shall comply with all notification obligations imposed by Applicable Data Protection Laws, including any obligations to notify regulatory authorities or affected individuals within the timeframes prescribed by law.
**[Article 9 --- Data Subject / Consumer Rights Cooperation]{.underline}**

**9.1 Assistance with Consumer Requests.** Vendor shall assist Company in fulfilling its obligations to respond to Consumer rights requests under Applicable Data Protection Laws, including but not limited to requests to know, access, correct, delete, port, and opt out of the sale or sharing of Personal Information, as well as requests to limit the use and disclosure of sensitive personal information. Vendor shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational processes to enable Company to comply with such Consumer requests in a timely and efficient manner.

**9.2 Notification of Direct Consumer Requests.** Vendor shall promptly, and in no event later than five (5) business days after receipt, notify Company if Vendor receives a Consumer rights request directly from a Consumer relating to Personal Information Processed on behalf of Company. Vendor shall not independently respond to, fulfill, or deny any such Consumer request unless directed to do so by Company in writing. Vendor shall refer the Consumer to Company for handling of the request, unless Company instructs otherwise.

**9.3 Systems and Processes for Consumer Requests.** Vendor shall maintain systems and processes capable of identifying, locating, retrieving, and, where applicable, deleting or correcting Personal Information by Consumer, in order to enable Company to respond to Consumer rights requests in compliance with the timeframes established by Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall ensure that its systems are designed to facilitate compliance with Company\'s obligations to respond to Consumer requests within forty-five (45) calendar days of receipt (or such other period as may be specified by Applicable Data Protection Laws), taking into account any extensions permitted by law.

**9.4 Identity Verification.** Vendor shall implement reasonable measures to verify the identity of Consumers submitting rights requests, in coordination with Company and in accordance with Company\'s identity verification procedures. Vendor shall not fulfill any Consumer request unless the identity of the requesting Consumer has been verified to Company\'s reasonable satisfaction. Vendor shall cooperate with Company in implementing and refining identity verification processes as needed.

**9.5 No Additional Fees.** Vendor shall not charge Company additional fees, surcharges, or other costs for assistance with Consumer rights requests that are part of Vendor\'s ordinary-course obligations under Applicable Data Protection Laws and this DPA. The Parties acknowledge that Vendor\'s obligation to assist with Consumer rights requests is an integral component of the services provided under the Agreement and is included in the fees paid by Company under the Agreement.
**[Article 10 --- De-Identification Standards]{.underline}**

**10.1 De-Identification Requirements.** If Vendor de-identifies Personal Information as part of the services provided under the Agreement, Vendor shall ensure that the de-identification process meets all requirements of Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m), and any other applicable statutory or regulatory definitions of de-identification, including the GLBA de-identification requirements where applicable. Vendor shall document its de-identification methodologies and make such documentation available to Company upon request.

**10.2 Technical Safeguards Against Re-Identification.** Vendor shall implement and maintain technical safeguards and business processes that are reasonably designed to prevent re-identification of De-Identified Data, including without limitation: (a) the removal or transformation of direct identifiers; (b) the suppression or generalization of quasi-identifiers to levels that prevent re-identification; (c) the application of appropriate statistical disclosure limitation techniques; and (d) access controls and use restrictions specific to De-Identified Data.

**10.3 Prohibition on Re-Identification.** Vendor shall not attempt to re-identify De-Identified Data, and shall contractually prohibit its Sub-Processors, employees, contractors, and agents from attempting to re-identify De-Identified Data. In the event that Vendor or any of its Sub-Processors, employees, contractors, or agents inadvertently re-identifies any De-Identified Data, Vendor shall: (a) immediately cease use of the re-identified data; (b) promptly notify Company; and (c) delete or re-de-identify the data in accordance with Company\'s instructions.

**10.4 Independent Verification.** Vendor shall subject any de-identification methodology to independent verification by a qualified professional (such as a statistician, data scientist, or privacy engineer with relevant expertise) before deploying such methodology in production. Vendor shall provide Company with a summary of the independent verification, including the methodology used, the conclusions reached, and any limitations identified, upon Company\'s request.

**10.5 Public Commitment.** Vendor shall make publicly available, such as in its privacy policy or on its website, a commitment to maintain and use De-Identified Data only in de-identified form and to not attempt to re-identify the data, as required by Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and any other Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall provide Company with a link to or copy of such public commitment upon request.

**10.6 Sub-Processor Obligations.** Any contractual obligations regarding De-Identified Data imposed on Sub-Processors engaged by Vendor shall be no less protective than those set forth in this Article 10. Vendor shall ensure that all Sub-Processors comply with the de-identification standards, technical safeguards, and prohibitions on re-identification set forth herein.
**[Article 11 --- Data Return and Deletion upon Termination]{.underline}**

**11.1 Data Return or Deletion.** Upon the expiration or termination of the Agreement (for any reason), or upon Company\'s earlier written request at any time during the term of the Agreement, Vendor shall, at Company\'s sole election, either: (a) return to Company all Personal Information in Vendor\'s possession or control, in a commonly used, structured, machine-readable format designated by Company, including all copies, backups, archives, and replications of Personal Information; or (b) securely delete and destroy all Personal Information in Vendor\'s possession or control, including all copies, backups, archives, and replications, using methods that render the Personal Information permanently unrecoverable. Company shall communicate its election to Vendor in writing.

**11.2 Timeframe for Return or Deletion.** Vendor shall complete the return or secure deletion and destruction of all Personal Information within thirty (30) days of receiving Company\'s instruction under Section 11.1. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to complete such return or deletion as promptly as practicable within such period. If Vendor requires additional time due to the volume or complexity of the data, Vendor shall notify Company in writing, specifying the additional time needed and the reasons therefor, and the Parties shall agree in writing on a revised timeline.

**11.3 Certification of Deletion or Return.** Upon completion of the return or deletion of Personal Information, Vendor shall provide Company with a written certification, signed by an authorized officer of Vendor, confirming that: (a) all Personal Information has been returned or deleted in accordance with Company\'s instructions and this DPA; (b) no copies, backups, archives, or replications of Personal Information remain in Vendor\'s possession or control, except as permitted under Section 11.4; and (c) Vendor has directed all Sub-Processors to comply with the data return and deletion obligations set forth in this Article. Vendor shall provide such certification within ten (10) business days of completing the return or deletion.

**11.4 Retention Exception.** Notwithstanding the foregoing, Vendor may retain Personal Information only to the extent that retention is required by Applicable Data Protection Laws, and only for the duration and purposes required by such laws. In the event Vendor retains any Personal Information pursuant to this Section 11.4, Vendor shall: (a) promptly notify Company in writing, identifying the specific Personal Information retained, the legal basis for retention, and the anticipated duration of retention; (b) continue to protect such retained Personal Information in accordance with the terms of this DPA; (c) limit Processing of such Personal Information to the purposes required by law; and (d) securely delete and destroy such Personal Information promptly upon the expiration of the applicable retention period.

**11.5 Sub-Processor Compliance.** Vendor shall ensure that all Sub-Processors comply with the data return and deletion obligations set forth in this Article 11. Vendor shall include in its Sub-Processor agreements provisions requiring Sub-Processors to return or delete Personal Information in accordance with Vendor\'s instructions, and Vendor shall obtain written certifications from Sub-Processors confirming compliance with such obligations.
**[Article 12 --- Audit and Inspection Rights]{.underline}**

**12.1 Information Availability.** Vendor shall make available to Company, upon reasonable request, all information reasonably necessary to demonstrate Vendor\'s compliance with this DPA and Applicable Data Protection Laws. Such information may include, without limitation, policies and procedures, training records, security assessment results, Data Breach records, Sub-Processor agreements, SOC 2 Type II reports, and other relevant documentation.

**12.2 Right to Conduct Audits.** Company, or its authorized third-party auditor (subject to reasonable confidentiality obligations acceptable to Vendor and not being a competitor of Vendor), shall have the right to conduct audits and inspections of Vendor\'s Processing activities, facilities, systems, and records related to the Processing of Personal Information under this DPA. Company shall provide Vendor with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any planned audit, specifying the scope, duration, and personnel involved. Vendor and Company shall cooperate in good faith to agree on the timing and logistics of any audit to minimize disruption to Vendor\'s operations.

**12.3 Frequency of Audits.** Audits may be conducted no more than once per calendar year, unless: (a) a Data Breach involving Company\'s Personal Information has occurred; (b) Company has reasonable grounds to believe that Vendor is materially non-compliant with this DPA or Applicable Data Protection Laws; or (c) an audit or investigation is required or requested by a regulatory authority with jurisdiction over Company or Vendor. In any of the circumstances described in clauses (a) through (c), Company may conduct additional audits as reasonably necessary, upon reasonable notice to Vendor, which notice may be shorter than the thirty (30) days specified in Section 12.2 in the case of urgent circumstances.

**Prohibition on Third-Party Model Training.** The vendor must be contractually prohibited from using TechNova customer data --- including any derivatives, transformations, embeddings, or representations thereof --- for training, improving, fine-tuning, or otherwise enhancing any models or algorithms for the benefit of third parties or for the benefit of the vendor\'s general-purpose product offerings. This prohibition must extend to all forms of the data, including de-identified or aggregated forms, unless a specific de-identification right has been negotiated in accordance with Section 4.3 below. This prohibition is absolute and non-negotiable.

In certain engagements, a vendor may seek the right to use de-identified or aggregated data derived from TechNova customer data for the purpose of improving the vendor\'s models, algorithms, or platform capabilities. TechNova may consider granting such a right, but only under the following conditions:

**Statutory Standard.** The de-identification must meet the statutory standard set forth in the CCPA at California Civil Code Section 1798.140(m). Specifically, the information must be information that cannot reasonably be used to infer information about, or otherwise be linked to, a particular consumer or household, provided that the vendor (a) has implemented technical safeguards and business processes that prohibit re-identification of the consumer to whom the information may pertain; (b) has implemented business processes to prevent inadvertent release of de-identified information; and (c) makes no attempt to re-identify the information.

**Independent Third-Party Verification.** The de-identification process and its compliance with the statutory standard must be verified by an independent third-party auditor. The auditor must be approved by TechNova in writing prior to the commencement of any audit. The auditor must provide a written certification that the de-identification meets the statutory standard, and this certification must be provided to TechNova before the vendor may make any use of the de-identified data.

**Classification.** Any de-identification right is within the Yellow zone only if both conditions above (statutory standard compliance and independent verification) are satisfied in full. If the vendor proposes a de-identification right without independent third-party verification, or if the proposed de-identification standard does not meet the CCPA statutory standard, the concession falls within the Red zone and requires VP Legal approval before acceptance.

Negotiating attorneys should be alert to vendor drafting that attempts to achieve a de facto controller relationship through indirect means, such as broadly defined business purposes, retained rights to \"aggregate\" or \"anonymized\" data without adequate de-identification standards, or carve-outs from the service-provider restrictions for \"product improvement\" or \"model training.\" Any such drafting should be redlined and replaced with the mandatory provisions described in Section 4.2.

For an agreement with annual fees of \$2,400,000, the minimum acceptable super-cap is \$7,200,000. This super-cap applies only to the IP indemnification and data breach carve-outs; the mandatory carve-outs for willful misconduct and gross negligence remain fully uncapped regardless.

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred latency commitment is a p95 response latency of no more than four hundred milliseconds (≤ 400 ms), measured at the vendor\'s API gateway for production inference requests. This threshold is required for real-time, customer-facing applications, including the LendStream product line and any other deployment that involves real-time decisioning, scoring, or response generation in interaction with end users.

**Yellow (Acceptable).** If the vendor cannot commit to ≤ 400 ms p95 latency, TechNova will accept a p95 response latency of no more than five hundred milliseconds (≤ 500 ms). A vendor offer in the range of 401--500 ms falls within the acceptable zone but below the preferred threshold. Negotiating attorneys should make a good-faith effort to secure a commitment at or below 400 ms before accepting a latency commitment in the 401--500 ms range.

If the vendor\'s best offer falls within the 401--500 ms range (e.g., 450 ms p95), the negotiating attorney should flag the offer to Product Engineering for confirmation that the specific use case can tolerate the additional latency. For example, a 450 ms commitment may be acceptable for batch processing or non-time-critical analytics, but may not be acceptable for LendStream real-time decisioning, where even 50 ms of additional latency can materially affect conversion rates and customer experience. Product Engineering confirmation should be documented in the negotiation file before the concession is accepted.

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any latency commitment above 500 ms p95 is a walk-away for customer-facing AI deployments. This threshold applies to any deployment that directly serves or interacts with TechNova\'s customers in real time. For internal-only, non-customer-facing deployments (e.g., internal analytics, back-office model inference), the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions may approve a latency commitment above 500 ms on a case-by-case basis, subject to Product Engineering\'s written confirmation that the higher latency does not impact customer experience.

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred model accuracy commitment is an F1 score of at least 0.95 on agreed benchmark datasets. The benchmark datasets must be mutually agreed upon at the time of contract execution and must be representative of TechNova\'s production data distribution. The F1 score should be calculated on the basis of the agreed evaluation methodology, including the specific precision and recall definitions applicable to TechNova\'s use case.

**Yellow (Acceptable).** TechNova will accept a model accuracy commitment with an F1 score of at least 0.92 on agreed benchmark datasets. An F1 score of 0.92 is the Playbook minimum; no accuracy commitment below this threshold is acceptable without escalation.

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any accuracy commitment below an F1 score of 0.92 is a walk-away. A vendor that cannot commit to at least F1 ≥ 0.92 on agreed benchmark datasets is not able to meet TechNova\'s minimum performance requirements.

**Yellow (Acceptable / Floor).** The minimum acceptable credit cap is twenty percent (20%) of monthly fees per month. For an agreement with monthly fees of \$200,000, the minimum acceptable monthly credit cap is \$40,000. This is a hard floor.

Every AI/ML vendor agreement must include a termination right that may be exercised by TechNova in the event of chronic SLA underperformance. Chronic underperformance is defined as a material SLA miss --- including uptime, latency, or accuracy failures --- in three (3) or more consecutive calendar months.

For latency, the negotiating attorney should push firmly for a commitment at or below 400 ms p95, especially for any deployment supporting the LendStream platform or other real-time consumer-facing products. If the vendor counters with a latency commitment between 400 ms and 500 ms, the negotiating attorney should coordinate with the VP of Product Engineering (currently Priya Anand) before accepting. Product Engineering\'s assessment of whether the specific use case can tolerate the proposed latency should be documented in the negotiation file.

For accuracy, an F1 score of 0.92 is the absolute minimum; the preferred threshold is 0.95. A stabilization ramp period is acceptable only if the post-stabilization target meets or exceeds the preferred threshold, and only if the agreement provides TechNova with a termination right if the target is not achieved by the end of the ramp period.

**Uncapped Carve-Outs**   Uncapped for willful misconduct, gross negligence, IP indemnity, and data breach                                                                        Uncapped for willful misconduct and gross negligence; super-cap ≥ 3× annual fees for IP indemnity and data breach                    Any cap on willful misconduct or gross negligence; super-cap below 3× annual fees

Iron Mountain IPM is TechNova\'s preferred escrow agent for all AI/ML vendor engagements requiring escrow deposits. Iron Mountain IPM has demonstrated experience in technology escrow and has developed specific capabilities for AI/ML model artifact escrow, including secure handling of large binary model weight files, structured deposit verification processes, and support for quarterly deposit update schedules. Iron Mountain IPM should be proposed as the escrow agent in every initial draft of an AI/ML vendor agreement that includes an escrow requirement.

**NCC Group plc.** NCC Group is an acceptable Tier 1 alternative escrow agent. NCC Group has a well-established technology escrow practice and has expanded its capabilities to include AI/ML model artifact deposits. NCC Group may be accepted as the escrow agent where the vendor has a pre-existing escrow relationship with NCC Group or where other circumstances make NCC Group a practical alternative.

**Other Providers.** Other technology escrow providers may be accepted as Tier 1 alternatives on a case-by-case basis, subject to the written approval of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions. Approval will be based on the following selection criteria:
> • **Standard Three-Party Agreement.** The provider must offer a standard three-party escrow agreement that is consistent with market practice and acceptable to TechNova\'s Legal Department.
Any proposed escrow agent that does not meet these criteria should not be accepted without escalation to the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions.

10                **De-Identification Requirements.** If the vendor has been granted any right to use de-identified or aggregated data, the DPA requires that de-identification meet the CCPA statutory standard (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m)) and that compliance be verified by an independent third-party auditor approved by TechNova prior to any use of the de-identified data.

15: **[Section 1 --- Purpose and Scope]{.underline}**
16: 
17: This Playbook governs all procurement of artificial intelligence and machine-learning vendor services by TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"TechNova\" or the \"Company\"). It establishes the mandatory negotiation positions, acceptable fallback concessions, and walk-away thresholds that must be followed by all personnel involved in the negotiation, drafting, review, and approval of AI/ML vendor agreements on behalf of TechNova.
18: 
19: This Playbook is jointly maintained by two departments within TechNova:
20: 
21: > • **Legal Department**, under the direction of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions (currently Derek Chalmers); and
22: >
23: > • **Product Engineering**, under the direction of the VP of Product Engineering (currently Priya Anand).
24: 
25: These two departments share responsibility for the ongoing development, revision, and dissemination of the Playbook, and all substantive updates require joint sign-off from both maintaining teams prior to publication.
26: 
27: Every AI/ML vendor agreement entered into by TechNova must be negotiated consistent with the positions, fallbacks, and walk-away thresholds set forth herein. No TechNova employee, attorney, or agent is authorized to accept terms that fall below the minimum thresholds established in this Playbook without following the escalation and approval procedures described in Section 2. Compliance with this Playbook is mandatory and will be reviewed as part of the Company\'s internal contract compliance program.
28: 
29: The scope of this Playbook extends to all AI/ML platform agreements, software-as-a-service (SaaS) agreements for AI/ML-enabled tools, model-as-a-service engagements, and any related vendor engagements in which TechNova procures AI or machine-learning capabilities from a third-party vendor. This includes, without limitation, engagements involving large language models, natural language processing platforms, computer vision services, predictive analytics engines, recommendation systems, and any other AI/ML-enabled product or service. The Playbook applies regardless of the TechNova business unit initiating the procurement, and regardless of whether the engagement is structured as a master services agreement, a standalone statement of work, an order form, or any other contractual vehicle.
30: 
31: This is Version 3.2 of the Playbook, effective as of March 2025. Version 3.2 supersedes all prior versions of this Playbook, including Version 3.1 (September 2024), Version 3.0 (March 2024), and all earlier iterations. In the event of any conflict between this Playbook and a prior version, this Playbook controls. A complete version history is set forth in Section 13.
32: 
33: **[Section 2 --- Decision Matrix and Escalation Procedures]{.underline}**
34: 
35: **2.1 --- Classification Framework**
36: 
37: To ensure consistency and clarity in vendor negotiations, this Playbook classifies every material negotiation term according to a three-tier classification framework. Each tier corresponds to a defined level of concession authority and escalation requirement. The three tiers are as follows:
38: 
39: **Green (Preferred Position).** The Green tier represents TechNova\'s standard opening position on each negotiation term. This is the position that should be proposed in every initial draft of a vendor agreement. Acceptance of a Green-tier position by the vendor requires no escalation and no additional approval beyond the negotiating attorney\'s standard authority. The Green position represents TechNova\'s optimal outcome and should be pursued vigorously before any fallback is offered.
40: 
41: **Yellow (Acceptable Fallback).** The Yellow tier represents a concession that falls within an acceptable range below TechNova\'s preferred position. A Yellow-tier concession is one that in-house counsel at the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions level may approve without further escalation. The Yellow tier defines the outer boundary of what TechNova considers a commercially reasonable compromise on a given term. Negotiating attorneys should document the business rationale for accepting a Yellow-tier position in the negotiation file but are not required to seek approval from the VP Legal or General Counsel.
42: 
43: **Red (Walk-Away / Escalation Required).** The Red tier represents a concession that approaches or breaches TechNova\'s minimum acceptable threshold on a given term. A Red-tier position is one that the Company should ordinarily decline. If a negotiating attorney determines that acceptance of a Red-tier position may be warranted by extraordinary business circumstances, that acceptance requires written approval from the VP Legal prior to execution of the agreement. The VP Legal\'s approval must be documented in the deal approval memorandum and must include a written business justification and a description of the risk-mitigation measures that will be implemented.
44: 
45: The following additional rules apply to Red-zone concessions:
46: 
47: > • Any single Red-zone concession on any term in a vendor agreement requires written approval from the VP Legal prior to execution.
48: >
49: > • Two or more simultaneous Red-zone concessions on any single vendor agreement require joint approval from the VP Legal and the General Counsel. In such cases, the deal approval memorandum must include an enhanced risk assessment and a written recommendation from the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions.
50: 
51: **2.2 --- Summary Decision Matrix**
52: 
53: The following table provides a summary-level decision matrix for each major term category addressed in this Playbook. Detailed negotiation guidance, including specific thresholds, examples, and fallback positions, is set forth in the referenced sections.
54:

57:   ------------------------------------ -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------
58:   IP Ownership & Licensing             Full ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations                                                                 Irrevocable perpetual license with portability, escrow, and non-assertion                      Less than perpetual license with 30-day extraction rights                                                             Section 3
59:
