**\"Customer Data\"** means all data, content, records, files, documents, and information of any kind provided by or on behalf of Customer to Vendor in connection with Customer\'s use of the Platform, including without limitation consumer nonpublic personal information (\"**NPPI**\") as defined under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act and its implementing regulations, personal information as defined under the CCPA/CPRA, and any other data that is uploaded, transmitted, or otherwise made available by Customer through or to the Platform.

**\"Customer-Trained Adaptations\"** means all fine-tuned weights, adapter layers (including without limitation low-rank adaptation (\"LoRA\") matrices), prompt-tuning parameters, and any other derivative model parameters generated through the training, fine-tuning, or adaptation of the Base Model using Customer Data or Customer-specific datasets. Customer-Trained Adaptations are the exclusive property of Customer.
**\"Data Processing Addendum\"** or **\"DPA\"** means the data processing addendum attached as Exhibit D, incorporating CCPA service-provider certification and GLBA compliance provisions.

**\"Derivative Models\"** means any models, model weights, algorithms, or improvements derived from, based upon, or incorporating any element of the Base Model, including without limitation whether created by Vendor, Customer, or any third party. For the avoidance of doubt, Derivative Models expressly exclude Customer-Trained Adaptations.

**\"Documentation\"** means Vendor\'s then-current technical and user documentation for the Platform, including API reference guides, integration specifications, user manuals, and release notes, as such documentation may be updated by Vendor from time to time during the Term and made available to Customer through Vendor\'s documentation portal or other delivery mechanism.
**\"Effective Date\"** means July 1, 2025.
**\"Escrow Agent\"** means Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. See Article 5A and Exhibit E.

**\"Escrow Materials\"** means the materials to be deposited into escrow pursuant to Section 5A.2, including (a) complete source code for the Base Model, (b) Customer-Trained Adaptations, (c) training configuration files and pipeline artifacts, and (d) all Documentation necessary to build, deploy, and operate the Platform.
**\"Feedback\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 5. 4.
**\"Fees\"** means all amounts payable by Customer to Vendor under this Agreement, including under Article 4 and any applicable Statement of Work.

**\"Go-Live\"** means the date on which the Platform is made available for production use by Customer following successful completion of the implementation and fine-tuning process described in Article 3 and the initial Statement of Work, targeted for October 1, 2025.
**\"Implementation Fee\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 4.2.

**\"Implementation Services\"** means the configuration, integration, fine-tuning, training, testing, and related professional services described in Article 3 and any applicable Statement of Work, including the initial Statement of Work attached hereto as Exhibit A.
**\"Included API Calls\"** means forty million (40,000,000) API calls per Contract Year, as further described in Section 4.3.
**\"Initial Term\"** means the period commencing on the Effective Date and ending on June 30, 2028, unless earlier terminated in accordance with Article 13.

**\"Intellectual Property Rights\"** means all patents, patent applications, copyrights, copyright registrations and applications, trademarks, trademark registrations and applications, trade secrets, know-how, inventions (whether or not patentable), moral rights, rights of publicity, database rights, and all other intellectual property and proprietary rights of any kind recognized in any jurisdiction worldwide, together with all applications, registrations, renewals, extensions, and restorations thereof.
**\"IP Claim\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 11.1.
**\"Overage Rate\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 4.3.
**\"Party\"** or **\"Parties\"** means Vendor and/or Customer, individually or collectively, as the context requires.

**\"Platform\"** means the MeridianIQ document processing platform, including the Base Model, all APIs, user interfaces, dashboards, analytics tools, and related infrastructure operated and maintained by Vendor and made available to Customer pursuant to this Agreement.
**\"Renewal Term\"** means each successive twelve (12)-month period following the expiration of the Initial Term, as further described in Section 13.2.
**\"Service Credits\"** means the credits available to Customer under Section 9.4 and Exhibit B in the event of a failure to meet the applicable service level commitments.
**\"Service Level Agreement\"** or **\"SLA\"** means the service level commitments set forth in Article 9 and Exhibit B attached hereto.
**\"Stabilization Period\"** means the ninety (90)-day period immediately following Go-Live.

**\"Statement of Work\"** or **\"SOW\"** means a statement of work executed by both Parties pursuant to Article 3 that describes the scope, deliverables, timeline, and fees for Implementation Services or other professional services to be performed by Vendor under this Agreement.
**\"Super-Cap\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 10.3.
**\"Term\"** means the Initial Term together with any Renewal Terms, as applicable.
**\"Uptime SLA\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 9.1.
**[ARTICLE 2 --- LICENSE GRANT AND SCOPE OF USE]{.underline}**
**Section 2.1 --- License Grant**

Subject to and conditioned upon Customer\'s compliance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including timely payment of all Fees, Vendor hereby grants to Customer a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable(except as permitted under Section 14.4), non-sublicensable (except to Affiliates) license during the Term to access and use the Platform solely for Customer\'s internal business operations in connection with Customer\'s lending technology product known as LendStream. The license granted hereunder includes the right to access and use the Platform through the APIs provided by Vendor, to submit Customer Data for processing through the Platform, and to receive and use the outputs generated by the Platform in connection with LendStream. This license is further conditioned on Customer\'s compliance with the Documentation and all applicable laws, rules, and regulations.
**Section 2.2 --- Scope of Authorized Use**

Customer may permit its employees, and authorized contractors who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in Article 7, to access and use the Platform on Customer\'s behalf and in furtherance of Customer\'s authorized use hereunder. Customer shall be responsible for all acts and omissions of its employees and authorized contractors in connection with their access to and use of the Platform. Use of the Platform is limited to the processing, analysis, and classification of Customer Data in support of LendStream\'s document processing workflows. Customer shall not use the Platform for any purpose other than as expressly authorized by this Agreement. Customer shall not exceed the Included API Calls in any Contract Year, except as subject to the overage charges set forth in Section 4.3.
**Section 2.3 --- Restrictions**
Customer acknowledges that the Platform and Base Model represent proprietary technology of Vendor. Customer shall not, and shall not permit any third party to:

> \(a\) reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, or otherwise attempt to derive the source code, algorithms, data structures, or underlying ideas of the Platform or the Base Model, except to the extent that such restriction is expressly prohibited by applicable law notwithstanding a contractual prohibition;

> \(b\) sublicense, sell, resell, lease, rent, loan, distribute, or otherwise make available the Platform or any component thereof to any third party, whether as a service bureau, managed service, or otherwise;

> \(c\) use the Platform or any output thereof for competitive benchmarking, competitive analysis, or to develop, train, or improve a product or service that competes with the Platform or any of Vendor\'s other products or services;
> \(d\) remove, obscure, alter, or deface any proprietary notices, labels, or marks on or in the Platform, the Documentation, or any output thereof;

> \(e\) access the Platform other than through the APIs and access mechanisms provided by Vendor, including without limitation by scraping, crawling, or using any automated means not expressly authorized by Vendor;

> \(f\) attempt to extract, reconstruct, distill, or reverse engineer model weights, architectures, training data, or any other proprietary components from the Platform, whether through prompt injection, model inversion, membership inference, or any other technique; or

> \(g\) use the Platform in any manner that violates applicable law or regulation, or that infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates the Intellectual Property Rights or other rights of any third party.
**Section 2.4 --- Reservation of Rights**

Except for the limited license expressly granted in Section 2.1, Vendor reserves all rights in and to the Platformand the Base Model (excluding Customer-Trained Adaptations), including all Intellectual Property Rights therein. No implied licenses are granted under this Agreement by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Customer\'s right to access and use the Platform is limited to the express license grant set forth in Section 2.1, and all other rights are expressly reserved by Vendor. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to grant Customer any right to access the source code or model weights of the Platform or the Base Model.
**[ARTICLE 3 --- IMPLEMENTATION AND TRAINING SERVICES]{.underline}**
**Section 3.1 --- Implementation Services**

Vendor shall perform the Implementation Services as described in the initial Statement of Work attached hereto as Exhibit A (the \"**Initial SOW**\") and any additional Statements of Work that may be executed by the Parties from time to time pursuant to this Article 3. The Implementation Services under the Initial SOW shall include, without limitation: (a) provisioning and configuration of Customer\'s dedicated Platform environment; (b) API integration of the Platform with Customer\'s LendStream product; (c) fine-tuning of the Base Model using Customer Data to optimize the Platform\'s performance for Customer\'s specific document processing requirements; (d) initial accuracy validation and testing of the fine-tuned model; and (e) initial training of Customer\'s designated personnel on the use and operation of the Platform. All Implementation Services shall be performed by Vendor personnel who are qualified and experienced in the relevant subject matter.
**Section 3.2 --- Implementation Milestones**
The Implementation Services shall be performed in accordance with the following milestones, as further described in Exhibit A:

> **Milestone 1 --- SOW Execution.** Execution of the Initial SOW by both Parties. Achievement of Milestone 1 shall trigger payment of the first installment of the Implementation Fee as set forth in Section 4.2(a).

> **Milestone 2 --- Go-Live.** Successful achievement of Go-Live, targeted for October 1, 2025, at which point the Platform shall be made available for production use by Customer. Achievement of Milestone 2 shall trigger payment of the second installment of the Implementation Fee as set forth in Section 4.2(b). Go-Live shall be conditioned upon the Platform performing materially in accordance with the Documentation, as mutually confirmed by the Parties through the acceptance process described in Exhibit A and Section 3.5.

Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve the targeted Go-Live date, but the targeted Go-Live date is an estimate only and shall not constitute a guaranteed delivery date. Delays caused by Customer\'s failure to fulfill its cooperation obligations under Section 3.3 shall extend the targeted Go-Live date by a commensurate period.
**Section 3.3 --- Customer Cooperation**

Customer acknowledges that Vendor\'s ability to perform the Implementation Services is dependent upon Customer\'s timely cooperation and assistance. Customer shall provide reasonable cooperation in connection with the Implementation Services, including without limitation: (a) timely provision of Customer Data in the format and quality reasonably specified by Vendor; (b) access to Customer\'s systems and environments as reasonably necessary for Vendor to perform API integration and testing; (c) designation of qualified Customer personnel with appropriate subject matter expertise to serve as points of contact and to participate in the implementation process, including providing timely feedback and approvals; and (d) such other cooperation as may be reasonably requested by Vendor and described in the applicable Statement of Work. Customer\'s failure to provide timely cooperation may result in delays in the Implementation Services, and Vendor shall not be responsible for any such delays to the extent caused by Customer\'s failure to perform its cooperation obligations under this Section 3.3.
**Section 3.4 --- Change Orders**

Any changes to the scope, timeline, deliverables, or fees for Implementation Services shall be documented in a mutually agreed written change order signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. No change to the Implementation Services shall be binding unless set forth in a duly executed change order. Each change order shall specify the nature of the change, any impact on the project timeline and milestones, and any additional fees associated with the change. Vendor shall not be obligated to perform any work outside the scope of an executed Statement of Work or change order.
\[ADDED: \### Section 3.5 --- Acceptance Testing

Following completion of implementation and prior to Go-Live, Vendor shall conduct acceptance testing in accordance with mutually agreed test plans and acceptance criteria set forth in the applicable Statement of Work. Customer shall have fifteen (15) business days to review acceptance test results and either accept or reject the deliverables with written specification of deficiencies. Vendor shall correct all material deficiencies and resubmit for acceptance within ten (10) business days. If Vendor fails to correct all material deficiencies after two (2) remediation cycles, Customer may escalate the matter pursuant to the dispute resolution procedures in Section 14.2 of this Agreement.\]
**[ARTICLE 4 --- FEES AND PAYMENT]{.underline}**
**Section 4.1 --- Annual Platform Fee**

In consideration of the license and access rights granted hereunder, Customer shall pay to Vendor an annual platform fee of Two Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,400,000) per Contract Year (the \"**Annual Platform Fee**\"). The Annual Platform Fee shall be invoiced by Vendor in equal monthly installments of Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$200,000) per month, with each monthly invoice due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice. Vendor shall issue monthly invoices on or about the first business day of each calendar month during the Term, beginning with the first calendar month following the Effective Date.
**Section 4.2 --- Implementation Fee**

In consideration of the Implementation Services described in Article 3 and Exhibit A, Customer shall pay to Vendor a one-time implementation and fine-tuning fee of Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$850,000) (the \"**Implementation Fee**\"). The Implementation Fee shall be payable in two (2) equal installments of Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000) each, as follows:

> \(a\) **First Installment.** Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000), due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice following execution of the Initial SOW (Milestone 1).
> \(b\) **Second Installment.** Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000), due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice following achievement of Go-Live (Milestone 2).
**Section 4.3 --- Overage Fees**

The Annual Platform Fee includes forty million (40,000,000) API calls per Contract Year (the \"**Included API Calls**\"). API calls made by Customer in excess of the Included API Calls during any Contract Year shall be invoiced by Vendor at a rate of twelve-thousandths of a dollar (\$0.012) per API call (the \"**Overage Rate**\"). Overage Fees shall be invoiced monthly in arrears, based on Vendor\'s metering and usage data for the applicable calendar month. Each such invoice shall include a summary of API call usage for the month, including the number of API calls consumed and the number of remaining Included API Calls for the applicable Contract Year. Overage Fee invoices shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice.
**Section 4.4 --- Taxes**

All Fees set forth in this Agreement are exclusive of any and all applicable taxes, duties, levies, or similar governmental charges (collectively, \"**Taxes**\"). Customer shall be responsible for, and shall pay, all sales, use, value-added, goods and services, withholding, and similar Taxes imposed on or in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, excluding taxes based on Vendor\'s net income, capital, or franchise taxes assessed against Vendor. If Vendor is required by law to collect any Taxes from Customer, Vendor shall include such Taxes on the applicable invoice and Customer shall remit payment of such Taxes together with the applicable Fees. If Customer is required to withhold any Taxes from amounts payable to Vendor, Customer shall gross up the payment so that Vendor receives the full amount of the invoiced Fees after deduction of such withholding Taxes.
**Section 4.5 --- Late Payments**

Any undisputed Fees not paid when due shall accrue interest at the lesser of (a) one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (18% per annum) or (b) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, from the date such payment was due until the date such payment is received in full by Vendor. In addition, Vendor may, upon at least fifteen (15) days\' prior written notice to Customer, suspend Customer\'s access to the Platform if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid for more than forty-five (45) days past its due date, and such suspension shall continue until all outstanding amounts, including accrued interest, have been paid in full. The foregoing remedies are in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other remedies available to Vendor under this Agreement or applicable law.
**Section 4.6 --- Total Contract Value**
For informational purposes and clarity, the total contract value for the Initial Term (exclusive of Overage Fees and Taxes) is as follows:
> \(a\) Annual Platform Fees for three (3) Contract Years: \$2,400,000 × 3 = **\$7,200,000**;
> \(b\) Implementation Fee (one-time): **\$850,000**;

The foregoing total contract value is an estimate for informational purposes only and does not include any Overage Fees, Taxes, or fees for additional Statements of Work that may be executed during the Term. The total contract value does not limit Vendor\'s right to invoice for Overage Fees or other amounts payable under this Agreement.
\[ADDED: \### Section 4.7 --- Right of Set-Off

Customer shall have the right to set off any amounts owed to Customer under this Agreement (including Service Credits under Article 9 and indemnification obligations under Article 11) against amounts payable by Customer to Vendor.\]
\[ADDED: \### Section 4.8 --- Audit Rights

Vendor shall maintain accurate books and records relating to overage calculations and API call volumes. Customer shall have the right, upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice, no more than once per Contract Year, to audit or have an independent third-party auditor audit Vendor\'s relevant records to verify the accuracy of invoiced overages. If an audit reveals an overcharge exceeding five percent (5%) of the audited amount, Vendor shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit and promptly refund the overcharge.\]

241: **12.4 Cooperation with Audits.** Vendor shall cooperate fully with all audits and inspections conducted under this Article, and shall provide Company and its authorized auditors with reasonable access to Vendor\'s relevant personnel, systems, facilities, documentation, and records. Vendor shall respond to all reasonable audit-related inquiries and requests for documentation within ten (10) business days of receipt, or such shorter period as may be reasonably necessary in the circumstances.

Company shall bear the fees and expenses of its own auditors and external consultants. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if an audit reveals material non-compliance by Vendor with this DPA or Applicable Data Protection Laws, Vendor shall reimburse Company for the reasonable costs and expenses of the audit, including the fees and expenses of Company\'s external auditors.

Within fifteen (15) business days of receiving Company\'s written notice of audit findings, Vendor shall provide Company with a detailed written remediation plan, including the specific actions to be taken, the responsible parties, and the anticipated timeline for completion. Vendor shall implement the remediation plan within the agreed-upon timeline and shall provide Company with evidence of completion. Company reserves the right to conduct a follow-up audit to verify that the identified deficiencies have been remediated.

Company may exercise such audit rights directly with respect to Sub-Processors, or may direct Vendor to conduct audits of its Sub-Processors on Company\'s behalf and provide Company with the results of such audits. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to include in its Sub-Processor agreements provisions granting Company (or Vendor, on Company\'s behalf) the right to audit the Sub-Processor\'s Processing activities related to Company\'s Personal Information.

249: **[Article 13 --- Cross-Border Transfer Mechanisms]{.underline}**
250: 
251: **13.1 Prohibition on Unauthorized Transfers.** Vendor shall not transfer, store, or Process Personal Information outside the United States without Company\'s prior written consent. For purposes of this Section, a \"transfer\" includes any access to Personal Information from a location outside the United States, whether by Vendor\'s personnel, Sub-Processors, or any third party acting on Vendor\'s behalf.
252: 
253: **13.2 Transfer Mechanisms.** Where cross-border transfers of Personal Information are authorized by Company in writing, Vendor shall ensure that appropriate transfer mechanisms are in place in compliance with Applicable Data Protection Laws prior to initiating any such transfer. Appropriate transfer mechanisms may include, as applicable: (a) the European Commission\'s Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs); (b) binding corporate rules approved by a competent supervisory authority; (c) an adequacy decision by the relevant regulatory authority; (d) the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, the UK Extension, or the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; or (e) any other recognized transfer mechanism under Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall document the transfer mechanism relied upon for each cross-border transfer and make such documentation available to Company upon request.
254: 
255: **13.3 Transfer Impact Assessment.** Where required by Applicable Data Protection Laws or by Company, Vendor shall conduct and document a transfer impact assessment evaluating the laws and practices of the destination country to determine whether they provide an adequate level of protection for Personal Information. Vendor shall make the transfer impact assessment available to Company upon request and shall cooperate with Company in evaluating the adequacy of protections in the destination country.
256: 
257: **13.4 Supplementary Measures.** Vendor shall implement supplementary technical, organizational, and contractual measures as necessary to ensure an essentially equivalent level of protection for Personal Information transferred outside the United States. Such supplementary measures may include, without limitation: (a) additional encryption or pseudonymization measures; (b) enhanced access controls and monitoring; (c) contractual commitments from the data importer regarding government access requests; and (d) restrictions on onward transfers. Vendor shall consult with Company regarding the selection and implementation of supplementary measures.
258: 
259: **13.5 Notification of Changes Affecting Transfers.** Vendor shall promptly notify Company in writing of any changes in law, regulation, government practice, or other circumstances in the destination country that may materially affect the legality, adequacy, or enforceability of the cross-border transfer mechanism in place, or that may impair Vendor\'s ability to comply with its obligations under this Article. Upon receipt of such notification, the Parties shall consult in good faith to identify and implement alternative transfer mechanisms or supplementary measures. If no adequate alternative can be identified, Company shall have the right to suspend or terminate the affected cross-border transfer and, if necessary, terminate the Agreement or the affected services thereunder in accordance with Section 4.4.

In the event of any conflict between the main body of this DPA and any exhibit or appendix hereto, the main body of this DPA shall control.

This DPA shall automatically terminate upon the termination or expiration of the Agreement, except that this DPA shall survive termination or expiration of the Agreement to the extent that Vendor retains any Personal Information in accordance with Section 11.4, and the obligations of confidentiality, data security, and data protection set forth herein shall continue to apply to any such retained Personal Information until such Personal Information is returned to Company or securely deleted and destroyed in accordance with Article 11.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Company may update Exhibit C (Processing Description) from time to time by providing written notice to Vendor, and Vendor shall comply with such updates, provided that any update that materially increases the scope of Vendor\'s Processing obligations shall be subject to mutual agreement.

331: This Exhibit A describes the Technical and Organizational Measures (\"TOMs\") implemented and maintained by Vendor to protect Personal Information against unauthorized or unlawful Processing and against accidental loss, destruction, damage, alteration, or disclosure. These measures are referenced in Article 5 of the DPA and form an integral part thereof. Vendor shall implement and maintain these measures throughout the term of the DPA and shall update them as necessary to address evolving threats, vulnerabilities, and industry best practices.

333: **A.2 Organizational Security Measures**
334: 
335: Vendor shall implement and maintain the following organizational security measures:
336: 
337: > \(a\) **Information Security Governance.** Vendor shall maintain a formal information security governance structure, including a designated Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) or equivalent security officer with responsibility for the development, implementation, oversight, and enforcement of Vendor\'s information security program. The security officer shall report to Vendor\'s senior management on a regular basis regarding the status of the information security program.
338: >
339: > \(b\) **Security Awareness Training.** Vendor shall provide regular security awareness training to all personnel who have access to Personal Information, including employees, contractors, and temporary staff. Training shall be provided upon onboarding and at least annually thereafter, and shall cover topics including data handling procedures, phishing awareness, password security, incident reporting, and Vendor\'s obligations under this DPA and Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall maintain records of training completion.
340: >
341: > \(c\) **Background Checks.** Vendor shall conduct background checks on all personnel who will have access to Personal Information, to the extent permitted by Applicable Data Protection Laws and consistent with the sensitivity of the Personal Information to be accessed. Background checks shall be conducted prior to granting access and shall be appropriate to the role and level of access.
342: >
343: > \(d\) **Information Security Policies and Procedures.** Vendor shall maintain documented information security policies and procedures that address, at a minimum, data classification, access control, incident response, acceptable use, data retention and destruction, change management, and third-party risk management. Policies and procedures shall be reviewed and updated at least annually, and more frequently as needed to address changes in Vendor\'s operations, threats, or Applicable Data Protection Laws.

345: **A.3 Technical Security Measures**
346: 
347: Vendor shall implement and maintain the following technical security measures:
348: 
349: > \(a\) **Encryption Standards.** All Personal Information stored by Vendor shall be encrypted at rest using AES-256 encryption or an equivalent or stronger standard. All Personal Information transmitted by Vendor shall be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher. Encryption key management practices shall follow industry best practices, including secure key generation, storage, rotation, and destruction.
350: >
351: > \(b\) **Access Control.** Vendor shall implement and maintain role-based access controls (RBAC) based on the principle of least privilege, ensuring that each user is granted only the minimum level of access necessary to perform their assigned duties. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) shall be required for all access to systems Processing Personal Information, including remote access and administrative access. lines.text: **12.4 Cooperation with Audits.** Vendor shall cooperate fully with all audits and inspections conducted under this Article, and shall provide Company and its authorized auditors with reasonable access to Vendor\'s relevant personnel, systems, facilities, documentation, and records. Vendor shall respond to all reasonable audit-related inquiries and requests for documentation within ten (10) business days of receipt, or such shorter period as may be reasonably necessary in the circumstances.

**12.5 Audit Costs.** Vendor shall bear its own internal costs of cooperating with audits conducted under this Article, including the costs of making personnel, systems, and documentation available to Company\'s auditors. Company shall bear the fees and expenses of its own auditors and external consultants. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if an audit reveals material non-compliance by Vendor with this DPA or Applicable Data Protection Laws, Vendor shall reimburse Company for the reasonable costs and expenses of the audit, including the fees and expenses of Company\'s external auditors.

**12.6 Remediation of Deficiencies.** Vendor shall promptly remediate any deficiencies, non-compliance, or security weaknesses identified during an audit conducted under this Article. Within fifteen (15) business days of receiving Company\'s written notice of audit findings, Vendor shall provide Company with a detailed written remediation plan, including the specific actions to be taken, the responsible parties, and the anticipated timeline for completion. Vendor shall implement the remediation plan within the agreed-upon timeline and shall provide Company with evidence of completion. Company reserves the right to conduct a follow-up audit to verify that the identified deficiencies have been remediated.

**12.7 Sub-Processor Audit Rights.** Company\'s audit rights under this Article extend to Sub-Processors engaged by Vendor to Process Personal Information on behalf of Company. Company may exercise such audit rights directly with respect to Sub-Processors, or may direct Vendor to conduct audits of its Sub-Processors on Company\'s behalf and provide Company with the results of such audits. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to include in its Sub-Processor agreements provisions granting Company (or Vendor, on Company\'s behalf) the right to audit the Sub-Processor\'s Processing activities related to Company\'s Personal Information.
**[Article 13 --- Cross-Border Transfer Mechanisms]{.underline}**

**13.1 Prohibition on Unauthorized Transfers.** Vendor shall not transfer, store, or Process Personal Information outside the United States without Company\'s prior written consent. For purposes of this Section, a \"transfer\" includes any access to Personal Information from a location outside the United States, whether by Vendor\'s personnel, Sub-Processors, or any third party acting on Vendor\'s behalf.

**13.2 Transfer Mechanisms.** Where cross-border transfers of Personal Information are authorized by Company in writing, Vendor shall ensure that appropriate transfer mechanisms are in place in compliance with Applicable Data Protection Laws prior to initiating any such transfer. Appropriate transfer mechanisms may include, as applicable: (a) the European Commission\'s Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs); (b) binding corporate rules approved by a competent supervisory authority; (c) an adequacy decision by the relevant regulatory authority; (d) the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, the UK Extension, or the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; or (e) any other recognized transfer mechanism under Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall document the transfer mechanism relied upon for each cross-border transfer and make such documentation available to Company upon request.

**13.3 Transfer Impact Assessment.** Where required by Applicable Data Protection Laws or by Company, Vendor shall conduct and document a transfer impact assessment evaluating the laws and practices of the destination country to determine whether they provide an adequate level of protection for Personal Information. Vendor shall make the transfer impact assessment available to Company upon request and shall cooperate with Company in evaluating the adequacy of protections in the destination country.

**13.4 Supplementary Measures.** Vendor shall implement supplementary technical, organizational, and contractual measures as necessary to ensure an essentially equivalent level of protection for Personal Information transferred outside the United States. Such supplementary measures may include, without limitation: (a) additional encryption or pseudonymization measures; (b) enhanced access controls and monitoring; (c) contractual commitments from the data importer regarding government access requests; and (d) restrictions on onward transfers. Vendor shall consult with Company regarding the selection and implementation of supplementary measures.

**13.5 Notification of Changes Affecting Transfers.** Vendor shall promptly notify Company in writing of any changes in law, regulation, government practice, or other circumstances in the destination country that may materially affect the legality, adequacy, or enforceability of the cross-border transfer mechanism in place, or that may impair Vendor\'s ability to comply with its obligations under this Article. Upon receipt of such notification, the Parties shall consult in good faith to identify and implement alternative transfer mechanisms or supplementary measures. If no adequate alternative can be identified, Company shall have the right to suspend or terminate the affected cross-border transfer and, if necessary, terminate the Agreement or the affected services thereunder in accordance with Section 4.4.
**[Article 14 --- General Provisions]{.underline}**

**14.1 Order of Precedence.** In the event of any conflict, inconsistency, or ambiguity between the provisions of this DPA and the provisions of the Agreement (including any schedules, exhibits, or amendments thereto), this DPA shall control and take precedence with respect to the Processing of Personal Information. In the event of any conflict between the main body of this DPA and any exhibit or appendix hereto, the main body of this DPA shall control.

**14.2 Term.** This DPA shall become effective upon the date last signed by the Parties below (or, if executed concurrently with the Agreement, upon the effective date of the Agreement) and shall remain in effect for the duration of the Agreement. This DPA shall automatically terminate upon the termination or expiration of the Agreement, except that this DPA shall survive termination or expiration of the Agreement to the extent that Vendor retains any Personal Information in accordance with Section 11.4, and the obligations of confidentiality, data security, and data protection set forth herein shall continue to apply to any such retained Personal Information until such Personal Information is returned to Company or securely deleted and destroyed in accordance with Article 11.

**14.3 Amendments.** This DPA may not be amended, modified, supplemented, or waived except by a written instrument duly executed by authorized representatives of both Parties. No oral agreement, course of dealing, or course of performance shall be deemed to amend, modify, or supplement this DPA. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Company may update Exhibit C (Processing Description) from time to time by providing written notice to Vendor, and Vendor shall comply with such updates, provided that any update that materially increases the scope of Vendor\'s Processing obligations shall be subject to mutual agreement.

**14.4 Governing Law.** This DPA shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of \[**\_\_\_**\], without regard to its conflict of laws principles, consistent with the governing law provision of the Agreement. Any legal action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this DPA shall be brought in the courts specified in the dispute resolution provision of the Agreement.

**14.5 Liability.** The liability of each Party under this DPA shall be subject to the limitations and exclusions of liability set forth in the Agreement; *provided, however*, that the following shall not be subject to any limitation or cap on liability set forth in the Agreement: (a) Vendor\'s indemnification obligations arising out of a Data Breach caused by Vendor\'s failure to comply with its obligations under this DPA; (b) Vendor\'s liability arising out of willful misconduct, gross negligence, or fraud; (c) Vendor\'s liability arising from unauthorized Processing, sale, or sharing of Personal Information in violation of this DPA or Applicable Data Protection Laws; (d) Vendor\'s indemnification obligations for regulatory fines, penalties, or enforcement actions resulting from Vendor\'s breach of this DPA; and (e) any liability that cannot be limited or excluded under Applicable Data Protection Laws.

**14.6 Severability.** If any provision of this DPA is found by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect the remaining provisions of this DPA, which shall remain in full force and effect. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace the invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision with a valid provision that most closely approximates the intent and economic effect of the original provision.

**14.7 Entire Agreement.** This DPA, together with the Agreement (including all schedules, exhibits, and amendments thereto) and the exhibits attached hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the Processing of Personal Information and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous negotiations, representations, warranties, commitments, offers, contracts, and writings relating to such subject matter, whether oral or written.

Part 248) and the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) (\"**GLBA**\"), to the extent applicable to the processing of NPPI; (b) the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020, Cal. Civ. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Vendor\'s security program shall include: (a) encryption of Customer Data in transit (using TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (using AES-256 or equivalent); (b) access controls, including multi-factor authentication, role-based access, and least-privilege principles; (c) regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing; (d) intrusion detection and prevention systems; (e) security incident response procedures; and (f) employee security awareness training. Vendor shall, upon Customer\'s reasonable request and no more than once per twelve (12)-month period, provide Customer with a summary of Vendor\'s then-current security measures and any SOC 2 Type II or equivalent audit reports covering Vendor\'s information security controls.

**[ARTICLE 9 --- SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS]{.underline}**
**Section 9.1 --- Uptime**

Vendor shall maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the \"**Uptime SLA**\"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
> **Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100**

For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"**Downtime**\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).

Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours\' advance written notice to Customer\'s designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
**Section 9.2 --- Latency**

Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.
**Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy**

Vendor shall maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above zero point ninety-four (F1 ≥ 0.94), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset established during the implementation process, following the conclusion of the Stabilization Period. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer\'s production document processing workloads.

During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.
**Section 9.4 --- Service Credits**

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA, API Latency target, or Model Accuracy target in any applicable measurement period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a \"**Service Credit**\"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the SLA failure occurred.

Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against Customer\'s next invoice(s) under this Agreement . If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed thirty percent (30%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year. Service Credits are not Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5.
\[ADDED: \### Section 9.5 --- Termination for Chronic SLA Failure

**Reviewing invoice terms**

The fee schedule mentions that invoicing is done annually in advance, but the prior draft had monthly invoices. I wonder if Section 4.1 needs correction to reflect the annual fee structure. While the email confirms the annual fee as $2.4 million, broken down monthly, it seems we need to ensure the terms align with the fee schedule. So, I'll update Section 4.1 to clarify that the total annual fee corresponds to the invoicing schedule but also allow for monthly installment calculations for SLA credits.

**Updating SOW and exhibits**

I need to focus on updating the initial term and auto-renewal details, and perhaps revise the DPA exhibit as well. Regarding the SOW, the current targets are F1 ≥ 0.90 with an acceptance go-live threshold of 0.90, but Draft 3 points to a desired 0.92 for stabilization. Since F1 should hit 0.92 at Go-Live and remain that way for the 90-day period, I’ll adjust the fine-tuning target and acceptance criteria accordingly in Exhibit B.

    r=etree.SubElement(parent, q('r'))
    t=etree.SubElement(r, q('delText' if deleted else 't'))
    if text[:1].isspace() or text[-1:].isspace(): t.set('{%s}space'%XML,'preserve')
    t.text=text

def tracked_para(p, new_text, author='Kirkstead & Yao LLP'):
    old=p_text(p)

    i=etree.SubElement(p, q('ins'))

def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr=cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); shd=tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None: shd=OxmlElement('w:shd'); tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'),fill)

def set_cell_text(cell,text,bold=False,color=None):
    cell.text=''
    p=cell.paragraphs[0]
    r=p.add_run(text); r.bold=bold
    if color: r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(*color)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)
    cell.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER

def add_table_borders(table):
    tblPr=table._tbl.tblPr
    borders=tblPr.first_child_found_in('w:tblBorders')
    if borders is None:
        borders=OxmlElement('w:tblBorders'); tblPr.append(borders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right','insideH','insideV'):
        tag='w:'+edge; el=borders.find(qn(tag))
        if el is None: el=OxmlElement(tag); borders.append(el)
        el.set(qn('w:val'),'single'); el.set(qn('w:sz'),'4'); el.set(qn('w:space'),'0'); el.set(qn('w:color'),'B7C9D6')

from zipfile import ZipFile, ZIP_DEFLATED
from lxml import etree
from copy import deepcopy

from docx.oxml.ns import qn

XML='http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace'
ns={'w':W}
q=lambda t: '{%s}%s'%(W,t)

SRC='documents/technova-ai-vendor-agreement-draft-2-redline.docx'
OUT='output'
Path(OUT).mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# -------- XML helpers --------
def accept_revisions(root):
    # Accept tracked insertions and reject tracked deletions from Draft 2.
    for tag in ['del','moveFrom']:
        for el in list(root.xpath('.//w:'+tag, namespaces=ns)):
            parent=el.getparent()
            if parent is not None: parent.remove(el)
    for tag in ['ins','moveTo']:
        for el in list(root.xpath('.//w:'+tag, namespaces=ns)):
            parent=el.getparent()
            if parent is None: continue
            idx=parent.index(el)
            for child in list(el):
                parent.insert(idx, child); idx += 1
            parent.remove(el)
    # Remove revision metadata that would make the accepted base look like a revision.
    for tag in ['trackRevisions','doNotTrackMoves','moveFromRangeStart','moveFromRangeEnd','moveToRangeStart','moveToRangeEnd']:
        for el in root.xpath('.//w:'+tag, namespaces=ns):
            p=el.getparent()
            if p is not None: p.remove(el)


def p_text(p):
    return ''.join(p.xpath('.//w:t/text()', namespaces=ns))

def sanitize_markers(text):
    # Draft 2 contains visible editorial tokens in some accepted paragraphs. Remove them
    # while preserving the accepted language.
    text=re.sub(r'\[DELETED:\s*([^\]]*)\]', '', text)
    text=re.sub(r'\[ADDED:\s*([^\]]*)\]', r'\1', text)
    text=text.replace('<!-- pagebreak -->','').replace('<!-- center -->','').replace('<!-- /center -->','')
    text=text.replace('\\###','###').replace('\\##','##')
    # Remove outer artifacts from inserted exhibit blocks.
    if text.startswith('[') and text.endswith(']') and text[1:].lstrip().startswith(('###','##')):
        text=text[1:-1]
    return text

def clear_runs_keep_ppr(p):
    for child in list(p):
        if child.tag != q('pPr'):
            p.remove(child)

def plain_para(p, text):
    clear_runs_keep_ppr(p)
    r=etree.SubElement(p, q('r'))
    t=etree.SubElement(r, q('t'))
    if text[:1].isspace() or text[-1:].isspace(): t.set('{%s}space'%XML,'preserve')
    t.text=text

def make_run(parent, text, deleted=False):
    r=etree.SubElement(parent, q('r'))
    t=etree.SubElement(r, q('delText' if deleted else 't'))
    if text[:1].isspace() or text[-1:].isspace(): t.set('{%s}space'%XML,'preserve')
    t.text=text
    return r

def tracked_para(p, new_text, author='Kirkstead & Yao LLP'):
    old=p_text(p)
    clear_runs_keep_ppr(p)
    rev_id='42'
    d=etree.SubElement(p, q('del'))
    d.set(q('id'), rev_id); d.set(q('author'), author); d.set(q('date'),'2025-05-14T17:00:00Z')
    make_run(d, old, deleted=True)
    i=etree.SubElement(p, q('ins'))
    i.set(q('id'),'43'); i.set(q('author'), author); i.set(q('date'),'2025-05-14T17:00:00Z')
    make_run(i, new_text, deleted=False)

def inserted_para(ref, text, before=False, author='Kirkstead & Yao LLP'):
    p=etree.Element(q('p'))
    ppr=ref.find(q('pPr'))
    if ppr is not None: p.append(deepcopy(ppr))
    i=etree.SubElement(p, q('ins'))
    i.set(q('id'),'44'); i.set(q('author'),author); i.set(q('date'),'2025-05-14T17:00:00Z')
    make_run(i,text,deleted=False)
    parent=ref.getparent(); idx=parent.index(ref)
    parent.insert(idx if before else idx+1,p)
    return p

def find_paras(root, needle=None, exact=None):
    out=[]
    for p in root.xpath('.//w:p', namespaces=ns):
        t=p_text(p)
        if exact is not None and t==exact: out.append(p)
        elif needle is not None and needle.lower() in t.lower(): out.append(p)
    return out

def find_one(root, needle=None, exact=None, occurrence=0):
    arr=find_paras(root,needle,exact)
    if len(arr)<=occurrence:

h=find_one(root,needle='Section 5.2 —')
tracked_para(h,'Section 5.2 — License to Customer-Trained Adaptations')
p1=find_one(root,needle='As between the Parties, Customer is and shall',occurrence=0)
tracked_para(p1,'''Vendor hereby grants to Customer an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up, non-exclusive license to access, use, reproduce, execute, modify, adapt, deploy, and create derivative works of the Customer-Trained Adaptations, including all fine-tuned adapter weights, adapter layers, LoRA matrices, prompt-tuning parameters, and related artifacts, for Customer's internal business purposes and in connection with LendStream. tracked_para(p2,'''Customer may export the Customer-Trained Adaptations through Vendor's API in an industry-standard machine-readable format, including ONNX, SafeTensors, or a mutually agreed equivalent, within thirty (30) days after termination or expiration. # Escrow: primary proposal with scope and release triggers.
tracked_para(find_one(root,needle='Vendor shall deposit and maintain current versions of the following Escrow Materials'),
'''Vendor shall deposit and maintain current versions of the following Escrow Materials: (a) all fine-tuned adapter weights and Customer-Trained Adaptations used in Customer's production environment; (b) all training configuration files, hyperparameters, and training scripts for those weights; (c) all pipeline artifacts, orchestration scripts, evaluation scripts, and workflow definitions reasonably necessary to reproduce or redeploy the fine-tuned model; and (d) a dependency manifest, README, and technical documentation sufficient for a qualified professional to use the deposited materials.     return ''.join(p.xpath('.//w:t/text()', namespaces=ns))

def sanitize_markers(text):
    # Draft 2 contains visible editorial tokens in some accepted paragraphs. Remove them
    # while preserving the accepted language.
    text=re.sub(r'\[DELETED:\s*([^\]]*)\]', '', text)
    text=re.sub(r'\[ADDED:\s*([^\]]*)\]', r'\1', text)
    text=text.replace('<!-- pagebreak -->','').replace('<!-- center -->','').replace('<!-- /center -->','')
    text=text.replace('\\###','###').replace('\\##','##')
    # Remove outer artifacts from inserted exhibit blocks.
    if text.startswith('[') and text.endswith(']') and text[1:].lstrip().startswith(('###','##')):
        text=text[1:-1]
    return text

def clear_runs_keep_ppr(p):
    for child in list(p):
        if child.tag != q('pPr'):
            p.remove(child)

def plain_para(p, text):
    clear_runs_keep_ppr(p)
    r=etree.SubElement(p, q('r'))
    t=etree.SubElement(r, q('t'))
    if text[:1].isspace() or text[-1:].isspace(): t.set('{%s}space'%XML,'preserve')
    t.text=text

def make_run(parent, text, deleted=False):
    r=etree.SubElement(parent, q('r'))
    t=etree.SubElement(r, q('delText' if deleted else 't'))
    if text[:1].isspace() or text[-1:].isspace(): t.set('{%s}space'%XML,'preserve')
    t.text=text
    return r

def tracked_para(p, new_text, author='Kirkstead & Yao LLP'):
    old=p_text(p)
    clear_runs_keep_ppr(p)
    rev_id='42'
    d=etree.SubElement(p, q('del'))
    d.set(q('id'), rev_id); d.set(q('author'), author); d.set(q('date'),'2025-05-14T17:00:00Z')
    make_run(d, old, deleted=True)
    i=etree.SubElement(p, q('ins'))
    i.set(q('id'),'43'); i.set(q('author'), author); i.set(q('date'),'2025-05-14T17:00:00Z')
    make_run(i, new_text, deleted=False)

def inserted_para(ref, text, before=False, author='Kirkstead & Yao LLP'):
    p=etree.Element(q('p'))
    ppr=ref.find(q('pPr'))
    if ppr is not None: p.append(deepcopy(ppr))
    i=etree.SubElement(p, q('ins'))
    i.set(q('id'),'44'); i.set(q('author'),author); i.set(q('date'),'2025-05-14T17:00:00Z')
    make_run(i,text,deleted=False)
    parent=ref.getparent(); idx=parent.index(ref)
    parent.insert(idx if before else idx+1,p)
    return p

def find_paras(root, needle=None, exact=None):
    out=[]
    for p in root.xpath('.//w:p', namespaces=ns):
        t=p_text(p)
        if exact is not None and t==exact: out.append(p)
        elif needle is not None and needle.lower() in t.lower(): out.append(p)
    return out

def find_one(root, needle=None, exact=None, occurrence=0):
    arr=find_paras(root,needle,exact)
    if len(arr)<=occurrence:
        raise RuntimeError(f'Could not find {needle or exact!r}; found {len(arr)}')
    return arr[occurrence]

def scrub_accepted(root):
    for p in root.xpath('.//w:p', namespaces=ns):
        txt=p_text(p)
        new=sanitize_markers(txt)
        if new!=txt:
            plain_para(p,new)
